articles.title: Conference Championship Tracker: Big 12 Title Game Set, Big Ten Still Open
articles.summary: Which teams are already in, and who still has a chance to play in the 2026 conference championship games.
articles.body: Before the College Football Playoff, there are conference championships. And the race for conference title games is on. While some conferences already have their title game set, like the Pac-12 and the ACC, others, like the Big Ten and the Mountain West, still have open matchups and multiple title-clinching paths. Georgia is headed back to the SEC title game and awaits its opponent, and undefeated Utah clinched its first Big 12 title berth since joining the conference. Here's a full list of all conference title games, and how to watch: Conference USA Championship Jacksonville St vs. Liberty The Gamecocks and the Flames both clinched their spots in the Conference USA title game. Jacksonville State returns to the conference title after falling to Kennesaw State last season, and Liberty makes their first appearance since its win in 2023 over New Mexico State. How To Watch: Friday, Dec. 4 at 7 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Sun Belt Championship Louisiana Tech vs. TBD Louisiana Tech has already clinched its spot in the title game, with Georgia Southern and James Madison on the brink of clinching in Week 13. How To Watch: Friday, Dec. 4 at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. Pac-12 Championship San Diego State vs. Boise State Boise State and San Diego State meet for the first Pac-12 title game since the conference expanded, as the Broncos look to avenge their 22-20 loss to SDSU, suffered in Week 12. How to Watch: Friday, Dec. 4 at 8 p.m. ET on CBS. Mountain West Championship TBD vs. TBD The race for the Mountain West title game remains open, with New Mexico and North Dakota State still in contention to clinch in Week 13. How To Watch: Friday, Dec. 4 at 9.m. ET on FOX. American Championship TBD vs. TBD The American Conference has a plethora of clinching scenarios ahead of the title game, with UTSA, Memphis, North Texas and East Carolina in contention for a championship spot. How To Watch: Saturday, Dec. 5 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC. Big 12 Championship Texas Tech vs. Utah Utah's 11-0 undefeated record led them to the Big 12 title game for the first time since joining the conference in 2023. Now, Utah knows its opponent: No. 11 Texas Tech, which got a 48-27 victory over on Thanksgiving night. How To Watch: Friday, Dec. 4 at 7 p.m. ET on ABC. ACC Championship Wake Forest vs. Miami Both Miami and Wake Forest enter the game 10-1 and will face each other in the title game for the very first time. How To Watch: Saturday, Dec. 5 at Noon ET on ABC. SEC Championship Georgia vs. TBD The No. 1-ranked Georgia Bulldogs clinched their spot in the SEC title game for the ninth time in 10 seasons. The Bulldogs' opponent is still up for grabs, with Tennessee, Texas and Alabama still in the mix. How To Watch: Saturday, Dec. 5 at 4 p.m. ET on ABC. Big Ten Championship TBD vs. TBD The race for the Big Ten title match is still open after both UCLA and Indiana lost in Week 12. Oregon, Ohio State, Iowa and USC are others who all have a shot at clinching in Week 13. How To Watch: Saturday, Dec. 5 at 8 p.m. ET on FOX. articles.title: Adam Copeland's luxury lifestyle beyond WWE: How the wrestling legend built his wealth through real estate, an impressive car collection, acting ventures, and life away from the ring
articles.summary: Explore how Adam Copeland, famously known as Edge, has built his wealth beyond WWE through real estate investments, luxury cars, acting, and a fulfilling family life.
articles.body: Adam Copeland has been making a name for himself for decades as one of pro wrestling’s most recognizable names, best known for his run as Edge in WWE. An 11-time world champion for most of his career before coming to All Elite Wrestling (AEW) in 2023, he has had major championships, memorable rivalries, and an amazing comeback from a career-threatening neck injury.Away from the wrestling ring, Copeland has developed interests in acting, fitness, and other commercial ventures. His reported property investments, collection of vehicles, and family lifestyle with Beth Phoenix offer another perspective on how the wrestling star has used his success outside the squared circle.Inside Adam Copeland's luxury lifestyle beyond WWEAccording to Celebrity Net Worth, Adam Copeland has an estimated net worth of $8 million. His fortune has primarily come from professional wrestling, acting appearances, and commercial partnerships. Other publications have presented higher estimates, including figures up to $14 million, but these figures have not been independently confirmed.Adam Copeland started his WWE career in the late 1990s and soon became one of the biggest draws for the promotion. Edge’s run saw him hold the world championship 11 times and make numerous major pay-per-view appearances. He retired in 2011 due to a neck injury, but made a surprise comeback in 2020.Adam Copeland's real estate and luxury car collectionOne of Adam Copeland's most notable reported property investments is his mountain estate in Asheville, North Carolina. According to Celebrity Net Worth, he purchased the four-acre property in July 2009 for approximately $1.4 million.The residence reportedly features a 4,000-square-foot log-cabin-style mansion. Its estimated value has reached around $3 million, although this is not a confirmed current market valuation. The property reflects his preference for a quieter lifestyle surrounded by nature.Copeland has also been linked to several performance vehicles and SUVs. His reported collection combines sports cars with practical vehicles suited to outdoor activities.Adam Copeland's business ventures and lifestyle beyond wrestlingProfessional wrestling is not Adam Copeland's only source of professional opportunities. He has developed an acting career with appearances in television series and films. His notable projects include Vikings, Haven, and The Flash. He also played Ares in Disney+’s Percy Jackson and the Olympians, bringing him to audiences outside of wrestling.He's been acting, which has become a big part of his career since he first retired from WWE and started looking for other ways to make a living.Adam Copeland has also dabbled in the fitness industry with Pure Plank, a core-training venture he created with longtime friend and wrestling tag-team partner Christian Cage, AKA Jay Reso.He has endorsed fitness and recovery products, including Iron Neck, a product designed to strengthen the neck. These interests connect with his personal experience recovering from a serious neck injury and returning to professional wrestling.His commercial partnerships have included brands such as Plunge, Rhone, and Rocket Money, although individual endorsement earnings have not been publicly disclosed.Away from professional commitments, Adam Copeland shares his life with fellow WWE Hall of Famer Beth Phoenix. The couple married in 2016 and have two daughters, Lyric and Ruby.The family has had a relatively private life, despite both parents having careers in professional wrestling. Adam Copeland has also spoken about fatherhood and raising his daughters, suggesting he has a lot to prove outside the ring.His passion for acting, fitness, family, and the outdoors speaks to how his career has evolved beyond championship wins.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joel Rodríguez: "Nos ha costado mucho ganarnos el respeto en la vela profesional"
articles.standfirst: El controlador de vuelo del equipo español de SailGP atiende a MARCA antes de la Gran Final de Abu Dabi y hace balance de la temporada
articles.summary: El controlador de vuelo del equipo español de SailGP atiende a MARCA antes de la Gran Final de Abu Dabi y hace balance de la temporada
articles.body: Joel Rodríguez (Las Palmas, 1997) es una de las piezas clave del éxito de 'Los Gallos', el equipo español de SailGP que este domingo buscará en Abu Dabi su segundo título, tras proclamarse campeón en 2024. El controlador de vuelo del F50 atiende a MARCA con la tranquilidad que le caracteriza antes del momento decisivo. PREGUNTA. Está a punto de acabar la mejor temporada del equipo. Sin embargo, empezaron sin poder competir en Perth por daños en el F50 en el entrenamiento. Al no puntuar, tocó remontar desde el primer Gran Premio. ¿Cómo recuerda ese momento? RESPUESTA. Fue duro porque habíamos estado entrenando en Perth dos o tres días antes de la rotura y nos sentíamos super fuertes. Fue una decepción brutal, un bajón muy grande. SailGP es una montaña rusa de emociones; es parte del juego porque es una carrera de fondo. Emocionalmente pasas de sentirte super bien a no tener ni barco de competir. Empiezas a pensar que no vas a llegar a la final porque se escapan los puntos y es difícil recuperarlos. Luego nos pasó en Nueva York con otra rotura... Pero estamos en la Gran Final y eso demuestra la solidez que hemos tenido en todas las condiciones y el ser capaces de estar en todas las finales menos en Valencia. P. Nueve podios de 12 posibles (3 victorias, 2 segundos y 4 terceros). ¿Cuál ha sido la clave de su regularidad? R. El primer punto clave es que llevamos tres años los mismos regatistas en los mismos roles y se nota porque el F50 es un barco muy difícil de replicar fuera, y con que podemos entrenar pocos días. Además, trabajamos mucho para entendernos todos y llegar a un consenso. Hacemos mucho hincapié en tener un pensamiento común aunque haya diversidad de ideas. Tenemos aún mucho margen de mejora. Hay trabajo infinito por hacer. P. Lograron el billete a la Gran Final de Abu Dabi a falta de dos eventos. ¿Cómo llegan a la cita clave? R. Esa tranquilidad nos permite preparar cosas específicas de cara a la Gran Final, entrenar cosas más arriesgadas y también preparar la táctica. P. ¿Qué es más difícil: controlar un F50 a más de 100 km/h o controlar los nervios cuando os jugáis el campeonato? R. (Sonríe). Depende de cada uno. Históricamente, a nosotros se nos dan bien los momentos importantes y críticos. En mi caso, me gusta la presión. P. Siempre le vemos tranquilo. ¿Es así o la procesión va por dentro? R. Me cuesta exteriorizar mis emociones, pero soy bastante tranquilo. Intento ver todo a largo plazo. Puede se que sea el más tranquilo de todo el equipo (se ríe). P. Australia y España son finalistas. Falta por conocer si el tercero será Suecia o Estados Unidos. ¿Dónde cree que puede estar la clave para ganar? R. En la salida, quien esté delante en la boya 1 tiene una probabilidad muy alta de ganar. Estamos estudiando por dónde se puede atacar mejor a los australianos. Aunque el tercero no esté decidido, también estamos estudiando a los dos que tienen opciones. P. Igual que en el fútbol cada Mundial equivale a una estrella en la camiseta, en SailGP se cose una Copa. ¿El objetivo es la segunda? R. Queremos ganar. Sabemos que es muy difícil, pero lo daremos todo. Como se suele decir, ser segundo o tercero no vale. P. En 2024 ya ganaron el título. ¿Qué aprendieron de la final de San Francisco que puedan aplicar para ésta? R. Te da experiencia, pero va a ser muy diferente porque desde entonces el barco ha cambiado los foils y se navega diferente. Y también serán distintas las condiciones, en Abu Dabi habrá poco viento. R. Ganar en 2024 fue un punto de inflexión. Entonces dieron la sorpresa, pero ahora son referentes y los rivales les estudian... R. Sí, todos los datos son compartidos entre todos los barcos. Somos los segundos en la liga, es lógico que nos miren. Nosotros estamos ahí porque hemos mirado mucho a los australianos. P. En la vela olímpica España siempre ha brillado, pero en la profesional la hegemonía era anglosajona hasta que llegaron ustedes. R. Sí, es muy positio para España. En vela olímpica, nuestro país siempre ha sido muy respetado, pero este mundo es muy anglosajón y los referentes siempre han sido Inglaterra, Australia y Nueva Zelanda. A nosotros nos ha costado mucho ganarnos el respeto por ser españoles o latinos, pero con méritos propios nos lo hemos ganado. P. ¿Se ven favoritos o dejáis ese papel a Australia, líder del Rolex SailGP Championship? R. Llegamos bastante igualados. La salida va a ser fundamental. A una regata puede pasar de todo. Hay que ganar a Australia en la salida y defender la posición porque en el recorrido es difícil pasarles, rinden muy bien. Hay que navegar el barco al cien por cien. P. ¿Les gusta el campo de regatas de Abu Dabi? R. Vamos a navegar por tercera vez en Abu Dabi, pero no en el mismo sitio, lo han cambiado para que haya más viento. Siempre hemos tenido mala suerte allí, pero estamos fuertes en todas las condiciones. En Ginebra ya ganamos con poco viento. P. ¿Se ha llegado a visualizar campeón? R. En mi caso cuando esa imagen aparece, la quito de mi cabeza. Y Simone, nuestro entrenador, es muy supersticioso. No se puede ni hablar de victoria. P. ¿Qué tienen 'Los Gallos' que 'no tienen otros equipos de SailGP? R. La mayoría nos conocemos desde las campañas olímpicas, estamos muy unidos y esa unión es clave. P. De hecho, esta temporada sólo se les ha resistido el podio en Valencia, en casa. ¿Les ha quedado una espinita? R. Sí, emocionalmente fue duro. Para mí es el evento en el que mejor hemos navegado y en el que menos errores cometimos, pero pagamos muy cara la mala salida del domingo. P. Su papel es controlador de vuelo en el barco. ¿Cómo explicaría su labor a alguien que no sepa de vela? R. Controlo el vuelo del barco ajustando los foils (hidroalas) que hacen que se sustente el barco por encima del agua. Ajusto su ángulo continuamente. P. ¿Cuántas decisiones toma por minuto durante una regata? R. Lo mío es mucho instinto, estoy continuamente intentando que el barco corra lo máximo posible. Mi campo de visión es muy pequeño, voy mirando, literal, casi por debajo del barco, no veo la regata, toda la información me viene de lo que escucho por los intercomunicadores. P. ¿Qué es lo más difícil de controlar: la altura, la velocidad o la estabilidad? R. Lo más difícil es la estabilidad porque puedes volar alto pero darte un castañazo. A veces es mejor tener menos altura pero si va estable te da más a largo plazo. Tengo que ser capaz de anticipar los cambios de rumbo y trimado. P. ¿Qué información recibe de los sensores (cada barco tiene 800) y cuánto le ayudan los datos para tomar decisiones a bordo? R. Lo que más miro es la altura del vuelo, el cabeceo del barco, la velocidad, la intensidad de viento y la posición de los foils.

articles.title: “It was just a matter of time,” Nicklas Backstrom congratulates Alex Ovechkin as Washington Capitals honor his NHL milestone
articles.summary: Alex Ovechkin becomes the Washington Capitals' all-time leader in assists, with a special ceremony honoring his achievement, while Nicklas Backstrom congratulates him on surpassing his record.
articles.body: Alex Ovechkin shared a memorable family moment as the Washington Capitals honored him for becoming the franchise's all-time leader in assists. The ceremony took place at Capital One Arena on Wednesday night, with his mother, Tatyana, wife Nastya and their sons, Sergei and Ilya, joining the celebration.The 41-year-old forward received a warm reception from Capitals fans, who chanted his nickname, "Ovi," as he arrived for the ceremony alongside the team's president of hockey operations, Brian MacLellan. A video tribute highlighting his memorable assists and contributions to Washington hockey was also shown on the arena's center-ice videoboard.Alex Ovechkin celebrates historic assist record with Washington CapitalsOvechkin became the Washington Capitals' all-time leader in assists on November 19, surpassing former teammate Nicklas Backstrom's previous franchise record. He reached the milestone by setting up Boone Jenner's third-period goal during Washington's 6-3 loss to the Buffalo Sabres.The assist was the 763rd of Ovechkin's NHL career. He subsequently added another assist in Boston on Saturday, taking his franchise-leading total to 764.The achievement further strengthened Ovechkin's position as one of the most influential players in Capitals history. He now leads the franchise in four major statistical categories: games played, goals, assists and points.What did Nicklas Backstrom say about Alex Ovechkin?Nicklas Backstrom congratulated his former teammate through a recorded message, acknowledging that Ovechkin's record-breaking achievement had been expected after their years together in Washington.Backstrom admitted that holding the franchise assist record had been special, but recognized that Ovechkin was always likely to surpass him.He said:"I just want to wish you congrats on becoming No. 1 in franchise history in assists, passing me. I'm not going to lie to you. It was very nice to have it for a couple years, but it was just a matter of time that you were going to beat it."Backstrom also expressed happiness for Ovechkin and their shared years as teammates. Although he could not attend the ceremony, his message became one of the memorable moments of the celebration.Brian MacLellan also presented Ovechkin with an oil painting created by Ottawa artist Tony Harris, depicting the two former Capitals teammates together. Backstrom had assisted on 279 of Ovechkin's goals, accounting for approximately 30% of his scoring total.How did Washington Capitals perform against Philadelphia Flyers?The Washington Capitals marked the occasion with a convincing 7-3 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers, ending a five-game losing streak.Seven different Washington players scored during the contest, while Alex Tuch contributed a goal and two assists. Goaltender Logan Thompson stopped 18 shots to help secure the win.Ovechkin, however, finished without a point and extended his goalless streak to 17 games, the longest such stretch of his career.Despite the personal scoring drought, the Capitals captain remained focused on the importance of securing the victory. Speaking after the game, Ovechkin said:"I think it's just very important for us mentally to get two points. Obviously, sometimes the bounces are not going our way. But we take it and we move on."The victory moved Washington to an 11-11-0 record, placing the team sixth in the Metropolitan Division at the time. The ceremony celebrated a major individual achievement, while the result offered the Capitals an important boost after a difficult stretch.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El enganche conquista Mutua Madrid Horse Week
articles.standfirst: La gran novedad deportiva de esta edición cautiva al público de IFEMA con el espectáculo de la Copa del Mundo FEI
articles.summary: La gran novedad deportiva de esta edición cautiva al público de IFEMA con el espectáculo de la Copa del Mundo FEI
articles.body: Velocidad, precisión, habilidad y emoción. El Enganche se ha convertido en uno de los grandes protagonistas de Mutua Madrid Horse Week 2026. La incorporación de esta disciplina al programa deportivo ha sido una de las grandes apuestas de la presente edición y su estreno en IFEMA no ha podido tener mejor acogida. El público vibró con el espectáculo de los mejores cocheros del mundo, que han llevado a la pista principal toda la intensidad de la Copa del Mundo FEI. Aunque todavía es una disciplina poco habitual en las grandes competiciones ecuestres de nuestro país, el Enganche ha encontrado en Madrid un escenario de excepción para acercarse a nuevos aficionados. Se trata de una modalidad que exige una extraordinaria compenetración entre el cochero y sus cuatro caballos, así como una combinación de técnica, reflejos y precisión para superar a gran velocidad los recorridos de conos y obstáculos. La convocatoria de Mutua Madrid Horse Week ha reunido a una participación de auténtico lujo, con cinco de los principales nombres del ranking internacional: el australiano Boyd Exell, siete veces campeón del mundo; el belga Dries Degrieck; la alemana Anna Sandmann; y los neerlandeses Bram Chardon y Koos de Ronde. Junto a ellos, la representación española ha corrido a cargo de Antonio Pérez Pedrajas, que ha tenido la oportunidad de estrenarse en una Copa del Mundo indoor de estas características, midiéndose por primera vez a algunas de las grandes figuras de la disciplina. La primera toma de contacto con la pista madrileña tuvo lugar el jueves, en una emocionante prueba clasificatoria que cerró la jornada inaugural del evento. El triunfo fue para Boyd Exell, que volvió a demostrar por qué es una de las grandes leyendas del Enganche internacional. El australiano impuso su experiencia y velocidad con un recorrido sobresaliente, marcando diferencias frente a sus rivales. Bram Chardon y Koos de Ronde completaron las tres primeras posiciones, mientras que Antonio Pérez Pedrajas finalizó quinto tras una destacada actuación. La competición continúa este viernes con la prueba puntuable para la Copa del Mundo FEI, en la que los mejores especialistas volverán a enfrentarse en busca de la victoria. Una nueva oportunidad para disfrutar de una disciplina que, en su primera aparición en Mutua Madrid Horse Week, ya se ha ganado un lugar destacado en el programa y, sobre todo, el aplauso del público de IFEMA.

articles.title: Week 12 Fantasy Football Start/Sit Advice: What to do with Chase Brown, Mike Evans, more players
articles.summary: Scott Pianowski plays traffic cop, offering start/sit lineup advice for some key players in fantasy football Week 12.
articles.body:
Start-sit decisions can be vexing for even the best of fantasy football managers. If you need help setting your fantasy football lineups, Scott Pianowski offers some assistance with his Week 12 traffic report.

RB Cam Skattebo at Colts : It's been speculated that the New York coaches aren't enamored with Skattebo, but sometimes you have to love the one you're with. Skattebo has collected 56 touches over the last three weeks, good for 291 total yards, and he's scored a couple of touchdowns. The Colts have the second-worst run defense, according to DVOA.

RB Ashton Jeanty at Browns : Jeanty looked like one of the busts of the year not long ago, but the Raiders have finally unlocked him, making use of Jeanty's skills outside the numbers. He's had more receiving yards than rushing yards in seven of his last eight starts, and look for that trend to continue at Cleveland. So long as your league uses some form of PPR scoring, Jeanty gets the checkmark.

RB Ollie Gordon II vs. Jets : When the Dolphins play a one-score game, Gordon is basically a lock for 15-plus touches. The Jets aren't likely to blow Miami out here — the Dolphins have been better on defense than expected — and New York has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points to opposing backs. Look for Gordon to break his touchdown slump as well.

TE T.J. Hockenson vs. Falcons : He missed the first Kirk Cousins reunion game, but Hockenson and Cousins were in sync last week, with Hockenson posting a 6-55-0 line on seven targets. That's a decent return in what's been a messy year for tight ends, and Hockenson's role looks secure in Week 12, with Jordan Addison (thumb) expected to be out for another week.

WR Antonio Williams at Cardinals : He finally broke his touchdown drought in Week 10, and then it was a 9-122-0 splash against Cincinnati on Monday. Jayden Daniels has started to warm up as well, and Arizona is a funnel defense to exploit (31st against the pass, per DVOA, and eighth against the rush).

WR Mike Evans vs. Seahawks : To roster Evans is to be tethered to your phone, nervously scrolling through the latest injury news. But if Evans (Achilles) can go Sunday, you start him, no matter that he's physically compromised and up against the nasty Seattle defense. The parameters were similar last week against Minnesota, and Evans smashed with a 6-109-1 performance.

QB Deshaun Watson vs. Raiders : If injuries or underperformance have you considering a QB streamer, Watson makes sense in this spot. He's been over 300 passing yards in three straight games and he's also starting to run proactively, with 49 yards last week and two ground scores in three games. Even if Watson himself doesn't play great, it's possible his talented group of pass-catchers can drag him to relevance.

WR Jordyn Tyson at Bengals : It's been a curious stop-and-start for Tyson in recent weeks — he saw 13 targets and 74% of the snaps two weeks back, then fell to five targets and 50% of snaps last week. With Tyler Shough in poor form and the Saints the NFL's worst first-quarter team, Tyson is a reactive, not proactive, option for Week 12.

QB Anthony Richardson Sr. vs. Giants : Understand that Richardson has zero floor, as he's made just 15 pro starts and several of them have been messy. He's completed just 50.6% of his passes and he's thrown more picks than touchdown passes. But rushing production from a quarterback is nectar of the fantasy gods, and maybe Richardson will outrun his mistakes Sunday.

RB Chase Brown vs. Saints : He's stuck on one rushing touchdown for the year and Samaje Perine's role seems to grow weekly. And it's not like Brown is Cincinnati's clock-killing guy — he hasn't seen more than 13 carries since Week 2. Brown's summer ADP is a sunk cost; we need to focus on his current production level as we make start-sit decisions.

RB Tony Pollard at Jaguars : Pollard has been a rushing star in four of his last five games, but the Jaguars were the one team to solve him (9-33-0 on the ground). The Titans did lean on Pollard as a pass-catcher in that game, but given that Pollard saw no receiving work last week, it's tricky to rely on that base. Pollard moves down to the RB3/flex bucket for Week 12, not an automatic fantasy start.

WR Ladd McConkey vs. Patriots : If Justin Herbert (concussion) is cleared to start, you can give McConkey a play against a slumping New England secondary. But if the Chargers have to lean on backup QB DJ Uiagalelei (seven career passes), the entire LAC passing game goes back on the restricted list.

articles.title: Week 12 Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's lineup advice
articles.summary: Boone takes you through his starts and sits to help your lineup for fantasy football in Week 12.
articles.body:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 12 rankings .

It's been an up-and-down season for Washington, but through it all Daniels has been a solid fantasy producer when he's been healthy. He's currently sitting as the QB8 in per game scoring (19.4 fppg) and has been trending up in recent weeks.

Now, his schedule is about to give him another boost. Daniels takes on the Cardinals and Titans over the next two weeks, which are the two best matchups for fantasy quarterbacks.

This week's opponent, Arizona, has allowed eight top-12 fantasy QB finishes in the first 11 weeks, with some of those coming against the likes of Drew Lock and Jameis Winston. Daniels is positioned for a spike week and is a top-five option at the position.

C.J. Stroud vs. Ravens – Stroud is a top-five fantasy QB on a per-game basis this season, with five top-10 results in his last seven outings. Houston is also at home for this one and projected for the fifth-most points this week. This is not the scary Baltimore defense of years past.

Kirk Cousins vs. Falcons – After making his first two starts with the Vikings on the road, Cousins gets to return to Minnesota for a revenge game with the Falcons. Atlanta is the eighth-easiest matchup for fantasy passers and has allowed huge top-three QB performances to Joe Burrow and Patrick Mahomes over the last two weeks.

Last week's down game for Skattebo was easy to predict, since he was facing the Jaguars' strong run defense.

Fortunately, the rudderless Colts present an excellent bounce-back spot. Indy is giving up the eighth-most fantasy points to running backs, but since trading DeForest Buckner, its allowed 159 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns to Bhayshul Tuten, 124 yards and a TD to Javonte Williams, 115 yards to Ollie Gordon II and 124 yards to David Montgomery.

Skattebo is going to run wild this weekend as a top-10 fantasy option at the position. I'm also not concerned about the displeasure of his head coach, John Harbaugh, since the Giants have no one else to lean on at the moment. Tyrone Tracy Jr. is still a couple of weeks away and Devin Singletary failed in his lone start a few weeks ago.

Breece Hall at Dolphins – Hall has posted 87 yards, 108 yards and 100 yards, respectively, in his three games since returning from injury. Now, he gets his easiest matchup yet with a Dolphins defense that's the sixth-most generous to fantasy RBs.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. vs. Titans – Bhayshul Tuten has played without practicing before this season, so we won't know his status for sure until the Jags rule him out. However, it's trending towards him resting this week, which would open up a major opportunity for Rodriguez. Jacksonville is 14.5-point favorites against a Tennessee team that's allowed at least 91 yards to each of the past five running backs it's faced.

Denzel Boston has missed the first two practices of the week and even if he suits up, he'll likely be at less than 100%. Meanwhile, Concepcion has been coming on lately with double-digit fantasy points in three of his last four games.

Next up is a Raiders defense that is the ninth-best opponent for fantasy wideouts. The matchup is even better for slot receivers, since Vegas is allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to them.

The Raiders also play man coverage at a high rate, which Concepcion excels against. We'll keep an eye on the weather forecast, but if we avoid a washout, Concepcion is ready to shine on Sunday Night Football.

Stefon Diggs/Antonio Williams at Cardinals – Arizona's defense is a good matchup for basically everyone it encounters, including being the 10th-softest opponent for fantasy WRs. Williams is coming off his best game of the season and Diggs has been a consistent weapon for Daniels, especially in the red zone.

Carnell Tate at Jaguars – The only way to attack the Jags defense is through the air and we've seen some notable receiver performances against them this season, including Titans wideout Elic Ayomanor, who put up 79 yards on 10 targets in their Week 10 matchup, when Tate was sidelined. The rookie has at least 58 yards in five of his last six games, with touchdowns in two of his past three outings.

Hockenson is the seventh-best fantasy tight end this season, with five top-10 weekly finishes.

I'd also argue we haven't even seen the best of him yet, since he missed Cousins' first start since returning to the Vikings and was on the road against a tough 49ers defense last week, when he still managed six catches for 55 yards.

Minnesota has the best fantasy playoff slate for tight ends and the third-easiest remaining schedule overall, beginning at home against the Falcons this week.

Chig Okonkwo at Cardinals – If it isn't clear, you should start your Commanders this week. That includes Okonkwo, who has at least 57 yards in four of his last five appearances and now gets an Arizona defense allowing the third-most points to his position.

Mike Gesicki vs. Saints – After a couple quieter weeks, Gesicki rebounded with a 5-77-0 stat line in a good matchup with the Commanders. He'll get another favorable spot this week against the Saints defense that's the sixth-friendliest opponent for tight ends.

Shough has only scored more than one touchdown in a single outing over the last two months. It's not all his fault. Injuries to the offensive line have played a big role, and there were some tough matchups mixed in during that stretch.

The Bengals won't make life easier on him. Since the Week 6 bye, Cincy has only let one quarterback reach 18 fantasy points.

With the Saints only sporting an implied team total around 20 points this week, it's hard to expect Shough to break his current disappointing streak on the road in Cincinnati.

Bryce Young at Buccaneers – Young's worst outing of the season came against the Bucs back in Week 7. Since then, he's only topped 17 fantasy points on one occasion. Tampa Bay is the fourth-toughest opponent for fantasy QBs and Tetairoa McMillan is dealing with a foot injury. Things aren't lining up for Young this week.

Sam Darnold at 49ers – Darnold's return is great news for the Seahawks, but he gets a difficult test against the Niners. It's also important to remember, Darnold is only a fantasy option against easier opponents. When he was healthy from Week 3 to Week 8, he was the QB17 in fppg with only one top-12 result.

Montgomery's 26-carry, 107-rushing-yard, three-catch, 17-receiving-yard performance in Week 11 was brought on by a perfect storm of teammates being sidelined and an opponent that's all but given up on the season.

While Baltimore's defense isn't what it used to be, the Ravens present a much stiffer challenge this week. Montgomery will also be rejoined in the backfield by Woody Marks, which means we won't see another 29-touch effort from the veteran.

Considering Montgomery failed to reach 50 scrimmage yards in any of his four outings before getting hurt, I'm skeptical that we'll see him come close to last week's stat line the rest of the year.

Travis Etienne Jr./Alvin Kamara at Bengals – Etienne managed a respectable 76 yards on 14 touches last week, but the majority of that came on a lumbering 46-yard run. This is still a committee backfield that will be hard to trust. Same goes for Kamara, who has scored an absurd three touchdowns on just seven touches over the last two weeks.

Tyler Allgeier/Bam Knight vs. Commanders – Washington's run defense has been solid this year and is allowing the 12th-fewest fantasy points to running backs. With Allgeier and Knight splitting touches and the Commanders projected as 6.5-point favorites, this isn't the week to look for a sneaky start in Arizona's backfield.

Egbuka hasn't topped 63 yards in a game this year and hasn't gone over 50 yards in any of his last five outings. Perhaps even more concerning is the fact he's seen just five targets each of the last two weeks.

Any hope that he may have been healthier coming off the bye was misguided and his two catches for 18 yards last week were the final sign that it isn't happening for Egbuka in 2026.

With the Panthers defense showing improvement under interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash, you can safely sit Egbuka this week.

Ladd McConkey vs. Patriots – Justin Herbert missed the first two practices of the week, which means he likely won't be clearing concussion protocol for this game. McConkey was already a risky play with Herbert under center and now he's a player to avoid with DJ Uiagalelei in line to start.

Deebo Samuel Sr. vs. Seahawks – Samuel has been living off big plays and when they don't occur, you get a stat line like last week's 47 scoreless yards. A matchup with Seattle is definitely not a spot to chase a big play, especially if Brock Purdy is at less than 100%.

The degree of difficulty gets cranked up for tight ends facing Minnesota. The Vikings are the second toughest matchup on paper for the position, but they also haven't let a tight end reach 40 yards against them in any of their last seven games.

Meanwhile, Pitts has been held under 30 yards in three of his last four appearances.

You should be able to find a better streaming option than Pitts this week.

Mark Andrews at Texans – Andrews fell back to earth after his resurgent eight-catch, 82-yard performance in Jacoby Brissett's first start with the Ravens. Be wary of streaming him against Houston, which is the toughest matchup for fantasy tight ends, only allowing one touchdown to the position all season.

Hunter Henry at Chargers – The loss of Drake Maye makes everyone in New England difficult to start in fantasy. Even with a revenge narrative in play, Henry should still be on your bench (or the waiver wire) this week.

articles.title: Key Fantasy Football Matchups to Exploit in Week 12
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Ray Garvin offers up some matchups to exploit in Week 12.
articles.body:
The last flex spot always takes longer than it should. One guy gets more touches. The other has the better matchup. Then there's the guy who scored twice on your bench last week and suddenly has you reconsidering everything.

This week, I'm looking at five players whose roles line up with what their opponents give up. It starts in Cleveland, where the Raiders offer a good spot for both Harold Fannin Jr. and Quinshon Judkins.

Harold Fannin Jr., TE/Quinshon Judkins, RB, Cleveland Browns vs. Las Vegas Raiders

Fannin has a great matchup against a Raiders defense that sees 29.1% of its targets allowed go to tight ends, the second-highest share in the league. That's a good spot for any tight end with a steady role. Fannin has been putting up wide receiver numbers.

He's averaging 94.5 receiving yards over his last four games and has caught at least six passes in three of them. Before Cleveland's bye, he went for seven catches and 91 yards against Houston. That's 12.6 half-PPR points without a touchdown. Think about how many weeks you've spent trying to find a tight end who might catch four passes.

Fannin went from limited Wednesday with a groin injury to an estimated full participant Thursday. As long as he's cleared for his usual workload, he's a TE1 against Las Vegas.

Judkins has a chance to get going against a Raiders defense that's allowing 5.06 yards per carry to running backs, the worst mark in the league. If you've watched him grind his way to 3.4 yards per carry this season, I get the hesitation. But this is the matchup to give him another shot.

Judkins has 22 red-zone carries this season, nine from inside the five. Against Houston before the bye, he managed just 38 rushing yards but still scored and added three catches for 33 yards. He had only 13 touches in that game, so I'm keeping the volume expectations reasonable. The combination of a soft run defense and carries inside the five is enough to play him as an RB2.

Ollie Gordon II, RB, Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets

We've already seen Gordon take advantage of this matchup. The last time he played the Jets, Miami gave Gordon 25 carries and he turned them into 103 yards and a touchdown. I'd take a sequel.

The Jets are allowing 4.62 yards per carry to running backs, which ranks 26th in the league. Gordon has gone four games without a touchdown, but he's handled 27 red-zone carries this season, including 10 from inside the five. Those are the touches I care about when deciding between two flex options.

Gordon ran for 69 yards on 11 carries last week, and he's caught just seven passes over his last four games. The workload can swing, but even if he lands well short of 25 carries this time, there's enough room to run against the Jets to play him as a flex with RB2 upside.

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders at Arizona Cardinals

Williams gets Arizona coming off the best game of his young career, and the Cardinals have allowed the 11th-most yards per target to perimeter receivers over their last five games. Nine catches on 11 targets for 122 yards against Cincinnati got everyone's attention Monday night. The part I'm buying is how often Williams was already on the field.

He's run a route on 91.5% of Washington's dropbacks since the Week 7 bye. Over that span, he's seen 18.9% of the targets and 23.4% of the first reads. His target share jumped to 31.4% against Cincinnati, and with Terry McLaurin out for the season, there's room for Williams to keep earning looks from Jayden Daniels.

Stefon Diggs is still involved, and Williams went for 25 and 42 receiving yards, respectively, in the two games before the breakout. But I'm comfortable playing him as a WR3 or flex against Arizona. If Daniels keeps looking for him early in the progression, he can give you WR2 production.

Justice Hill, RB, Baltimore Ravens at Houston Texans

Hill's matchup with Houston fits what he does best. The Texans have faced 65 targets to running backs this season, the ninth-most in the league, and Hill has caught at least three passes in every game since Week 6.

The 69 rushing yards and a touchdown on six carries against Carolina probably got your attention. The four catches for 27 yards are what I'd carry into this week. Hill has 12 catches over his last three appearances, and if Baltimore has to chase points, that receiving role gives him a way to stay involved.

Derrick Henry returned to full practice Thursday after a concussion, and I'm expecting him to handle the bulk of the carries and the goal-line work if he plays. That leaves Hill as a deeper half-PPR flex. If I'm choosing between Hill and a back who needs a touchdown to give me anything, I'll take the catches.

articles.title: Kantserov Receives Well-Deserved Respect From Remarkable Road Trip
articles.summary: Chicago Blackhawks rookie Roman Kantserov is garnering well-deserved respect for his extraordinary first 25 games as an NHL forward. After […]
articles.body:
Chicago Blackhawks rookie Roman Kantserov is garnering well-deserved respect for his extraordinary first 25 games as an NHL forward. After a six-goal and eight-point three-game Pacific Northwest road trip, Kantserov was named the NHLPA's Player of the Week on Friday (Nov. 20-26).

Roman Kantserov is staying hot 🔥 The @NHLBlackhawks forward is currently leading all rookies in overall goals and led the league in points this week to secure his spot as NHLPA Player of the Week! pic.twitter.com/akdkK3djzk — NHLPA (@NHLPA) November 27, 2026

Roman Kantserov is staying hot 🔥 The @NHLBlackhawks forward is currently leading all rookies in overall goals and led the league in points this week to secure his spot as NHLPA Player of the Week! pic.twitter.com/akdkK3djzk

Kantserov recorded three straight multi-point games during the road trip, including his first NHL hat trick and four-point game against the Vancouver Canucks on Sunday. Three days later, Kantserov added two more goals in a 3-1 win over the Seattle Kraken , including the game-winner in the third period.

He led the league with eight points, six goals, and three power-play tallies last week, while his four power-play points and three even-strength goals were tied for the league lead.

The 22-year-old's transition from the KHL in Russia to the NHL has been seamless, as he currently leads the Blackhawks and all NHL rookies with 15 goals and 20 points this season. Kantserov also has more even-strength tallies (10) than any other first-year player has in total goals.

Kantserov's stunning first 25 appearances have put him in some special conversations. He's the first Blackhawks skater in the modern era to record 15 goals in his first 25 games, with Bill Mosienko last achieving the feat for Chicago way back in 1943-44.

With 10 goals in 11 games in November, Kantserov has tied Alex DeBrincat (Nov. 2017) & Dominik Kubalik (Jan. 2020) for the most by a Blackhawks rookie in a calendar month. With three more games on the schedule for the Blackhawks before December, Kantserov will have a chance to jump DeBrincat and Kubalik for the franchise's record.

Kantserov is also only the seventh rookie in NHL history to record nine road goals in a single calendar month, joining Glenn Anderson, Peter Stastny, Logan Couture, Dale Hawerchuk, Jimmy Herberts and Joe Malone.

Additionally, Kantserov became the third NHL player in the past 30 years to score 15 goals in his first 25 games, joining fellow future Hall of Fame Russians Alex Ovechkin (2005-06) and Evgeni Malkin (2006-07).

Before captain Connor Bedard re- injured his right shoulder on Nov. 17, Kantserov was his most consistent linemate, and the superstar's absence not only figured to crush the Blackhawks' competitive chances, but also Kantserov's Calder Trophy hopes.

But Kantserov hasn't slowed down one bit without Bedard. He's impressively increased his production while filling in as the Blackhawks' top-line center and carried the team to a 3-0 road trip.

During his final season in Russia, Kantserov made KHL history, becoming the first player 21 or younger to lead the league in goals and average over a point-per-game for an entire season. Now in North America with the Blackhawks, Kantserov has put himself in rarefied air once again, but now on the highest stage in the world.

Despite Bedard undergoing another shoulder surgery, Kantserov is giving Blackhawks fans something to be excited about and hopeful for amid a tumultuous first quarter of the 2026-27 season.

articles.title: 35 años de la histórica victoria de Undertaker sobre Hulk Hogan con la ayuda de Ric Flair... y Pablito Terrores
articles.standfirst: El 'Enterrador' se proclamó por primera vez campeón de WWF gracias a este triunfo. Hogan se quejó de que Taker le lesionó el cuello al hacer el Tombstone
articles.summary: El 'Enterrador' se proclamó por primera vez campeón de WWF gracias a este triunfo. Hogan se quejó de que Taker le lesionó el cuello al hacer el Tombstone
articles.body: Survivor Series, un evento de WWF celebrado el 27 de noviembre de 1991 en la víspera del Día de Acción de Gracias estadounidense, concitó mucha atención gracias a una cartelera que encabezaban Hulk Hogan y Undertaker, que aquel día se disputaban el campeonato mundial de WWF que ostentaba el primero. El ‘Enterrador’ había debutado hacía justo hacía un año en la compañía y su popularidad había subido como la espuma gracias a un personaje al que fue capaz de dar vida durante nada menos que 30 años. No había mejor combate que enfrentarlo al campeón e ídolo de masas, el inolvidable Hulk Hogan. Dos colosos frente a frente en la clásica batalla entre el bueno y el malo para un evento de Pago Por Visión. Fue una pelea que duró 15 minutos incluyendo unas presentaciones que fueron rápidas porque Taker recibió a Hogan en el ring a golpes. En el desenlace estuvieron involucrados tanto Pablito Terrores -mánager y portavoz del Enterrador- como Ric Flair, quien apenas llevaba un par meses en WWF y también ejercía de villano. El caso es que Flair colocó una silla para que Undertaker aplicara su característico Tombstone sobre la misma –aunque en realidad sin llegar a tocarla- y la acción quizás no salió como se esperaba, pues Hulk Hogan se lesionó el cuello y tuvo que pasar por el hospital. De hecho, en el ring se le vio algo aturdido tras la acción final con la que el Enterrador se proclamó por primera vez campeón de WWF. Undertaker, cuyo nombre real es Mark Calaway, explicó en 2020 a ESPN que Hogan le había dicho que ya tenía una lesión en el cuello y que le preocupaba recibir el Tombstone; también comentó que ese día, cada vez que se veían, Hulk le señalaba el cuello. En cuanto Taker hizo el Tombstone, escuchó a su oponente decir: "Ay, me has dado, hermano". La acción fue limpia, sin que la cabeza tocara la colchoneta y la silla, pero The Hulkster explicó después a su rival: “Lo que pasó fue que me apretaste tanto que no tenía espacio para moverme, y eso fue lo que me hizo daño en el cuello”. Gajes de un oficio peligroso para la integridad física.

articles.title: Phil Taylor says he is quitting competitive darts for good as he and Adrian Lewis are knocked out of MODUS Super Series
articles.summary: Phil Taylor retired from professional darts in 2018; he came out of retirement for this week's MODUS Super Series International Pairs, teaming up with friend Adrian Lewis; the Pair finished second-bottom in group C and were knocked out of the event
articles.body:
The 16-time world champion was lured back to the oche for this year's MODUS Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth alongside his long-time friend Adrian Lewis.

The English duo lost all five of their matches on Thursday but rebounded on Friday, winning three and losing two matches, to finish second-bottom in the Group C standings.

Taylor, 67, retired from the competitive circuit in 2018, five years after winning his final world crown, and when asked if he would make another comeback, the 14-time PDC World Championship winner told Pluto TV : "[This is] proper retirement."

A heartwarming moment unfolded after Taylor and Lewis were beaten 4-3 in their final group match against Scotland, as each of the other nations arrived to give Taylor a guard of honour, as he walked away from the oche.

"I mean I'm 67, I get my pension next February," Taylor said, when asked if this would be his last competitive appearance. "I'm a pensioner now, officially!"

"I'll still do personal appearances, more having a chat with people, talking about my career, that kind of thing."

Taylor and Lewis, who teamed up to win four World Cup of Darts titles between 2012 and 2016, finished Thursday at the bottom of Group C. Friday started poorly for the Englishmen, losing to Denmark's Ivan Springborg-Poulsen and Andreas Toft Jørgensen 4-2.

Speaking on his retirement U-turn this week, Taylor said: "I was dreading it to be honest with you because I know I wasn't playing like I can do, but now I've been here and it's all over, I've loved it."

The pair hit back on Friday with a 4-3 win against Germany, then beat Switzerland and Sweden, both 4-2.

The Englishmen would tie Scotland at three legs apiece in his final competitive match, before Taylor missed a checkout for 48 for victory, in what would have been a fairy-tale finish.

"Looking back now, it's like it never happened," Taylor said, reflecting on his glittering career.

"I've said to other people who have been on stage and retired: 'How do you feel now?'

"'It's like you've never been there'. It's ever so weird. And you come up on YouTube and you just go: "No, I know. I know I was there, but I can't remember it."

"It's very, very strange because, mentally-wise, you move on. That was your former life and now my life is different."

Instead of flying around the world competing, Taylor says retirement has allowed him to spend more time with his grandchildren.

"I've got 11 grandchildren," Taylor said. "So I spend a lot of time with them now.

"[I do] things I've never done before. Go to bed when I want; I go to bed early. For me, 9pm would be like, I'd be asleep two hours before 9pm, and it's great.

"I love getting up early as well. We can do all the chores. We can go shopping and get everything done, and it isn't even 11am. It's great!

"People say I'm the GOAT [Greatest of All Time]-I'm an old goat now!"

articles.title: Kevin Viveros tiene nuevo equipo en Europa y le deja varios millones a Atlético Nacional
articles.standfirst: Kevin Viveros da el salto a Europa: fichaje de 27 millones y contrato hasta 2030
articles.summary: Kevin Viveros da el salto a Europa: fichaje de 27 millones y contrato hasta 2030
articles.body: El mercado de fichajes europeo vuelve a mirar con fuerza hacia el talento colombiano con una operación de alto impacto económico y deportivo: Kevin Viveros está a un paso de dar el salto al fútbol ruso para vestir la camiseta del CSKA Moscú, en un movimiento valorado en 27 millones de dólares (20 millones fijos más 7 millones en bonos) y con un contrato proyectado hasta 2030. De acuerdo con los reportes periodísticos sobre la operación, existe un principio de acuerdo entre Athletico Paranaense y el CSKA Moscú para transferir al delantero colombiano de 26 años. La estructura financiera contempla 20 millones de dólares garantizados y 7 millones adicionales sujetos a variables y bonos, alcanzando así la cifra total de 27 millones de dólares. El acuerdo contractual se proyecta por cuatro temporadas, hasta 2030, lo que representaría una apuesta a largo plazo por parte del club moscovita para reforzar su frente de ataque. Aunque las bases de la transferencia entre clubes están encaminadas, restan ajustes finales en las condiciones salariales del futbolista para sellar la firma definitiva. La eventual transferencia no solo mueve el mercado internacional, sino que también tiene repercusiones directas en el fútbol profesional colombiano. Atlético Nacional, club por el que Viveros pasó entre 2024 y mediados de 2025 antes de marcharse a Brasil, conserva un porcentaje de la operación (reportado en un 30 %), por lo que recibiría un ingreso significativo si se concreta el traspaso. Para el conjunto verdolaga, este tipo de ventas ratifica la importancia de estructurar porcentajes de futura transferencia al negociar futbolistas hacia ligas sudamericanas con mayor poder adquisitivo, convirtiendo el rendimiento posterior del jugador en un retorno económico relevante. El interés europeo responde a una temporada sobresaliente de Kevin Viveros con Athletico Paranaense en 2026: Protagonismo en el Brasileirao: El atacante se consolidó como máximo goleador del campeonato brasileño, acumulando 21 anotaciones en la liga doméstica y superando la barrera de los 20 goles en el año calendario sumando todas las competencias. Aporte ofensivo integral: Más allá de definir jugadas, su producción combinó goles y asistencias para sostener el poder ofensivo de su equipo a lo largo de la campaña. Regreso a la Tricolor: Su regularidad en Brasil le abrió nuevamente las puertas de la Selección Colombia bajo el ciclo de Néstor Lorenzo, sumando minutos en amistosos internacionales frente a selecciones como México, Paraguay y Perú. Esta operación marcaría el retorno de Viveros a Europa tras su paso previo por el FK Sarajevo en Bosnia y Herzegovina. Llegar al CSKA Moscú implica adaptarse a un entorno competitivo exigente, con cambios climáticos marcados, un calendario de alta intensidad física y la presión de responder con goles en un club histórico de la Liga Premier de Rusia.

articles.summary: Tulio Gómez abre el debate: la verdadera batalla por la TV del fútbol colombiano no es solo quién transmite, sino cómo se reparte el dinero
articles.body: La disputa por los derechos de televisión del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano entró en una fase decisiva. Aunque gran parte de la atención se concentró en saber si Win Sports conservaría el contrato desde 2027, el dueño del América de Cali, Tulio Gómez, dejó claro que el punto más sensible para los clubes no es únicamente el operador que transmitirá los partidos, sino la fórmula con la que se distribuirán los recursos entre los 36 equipos afiliados a la Dimayor. “Ninguno de los 36 equipos nos estamos oponiendo a esa oferta. Win tiene el derecho de preferencia y si lo igualó o lo superó, será quien se quede con el contrato”, afirmó Gómez. Su mensaje buscó desactivar la idea de que los clubes estén bloqueando una eventual continuidad de Win Sports: la discusión real, dijo, está en el reparto económico del nuevo acuerdo. El proceso tomó un giro relevante en septiembre de 2026, cuando la Dimayor recibió una propuesta externa por los derechos audiovisuales del FPC a partir de 2027. La oferta, atribuida a un grupo vinculado a Mauricio Correa, rondaría los 90 millones de dólares anuales, una cifra que marcó un nuevo estándar en la negociación del fútbol colombiano. Win Sports, operador que ostenta los derechos desde 2012, contaba con una cláusula de preferencia que le permitía igualar o superar esa oferta antes del 21 de noviembre. Varios reportes indicaron que la compañía no solo igualó el monto, sino que lo habría mejorado ligeramente, lo que la dejaría en posición de mantener el contrato. Sin embargo, la Dimayor no había emitido un comunicado oficial que confirmara la decisión definitiva. El proceso sigue involucrando aspectos que van más allá del valor económico: calendario de pagos, condiciones de producción, distribución de contenidos, plataformas digitales, mercados internacionales y demás obligaciones contractuales. Las declaraciones de Gómez tienen una lectura política dentro de la dirigencia del fútbol colombiano. Al reconocer que ningún club se opone a la oferta, el máximo accionista del América de Cali dejó entrever que la eventual permanencia de Win Sports no sería, en principio, el obstáculo central. “Lo que estamos discutiendo es la distribución de los recursos del nuevo contrato y esperamos llegar en consenso a una fórmula que nos satisfaga a todos”, expresó el dirigente. Esa frase resume el conflicto de fondo. Para los clubes, un contrato más valioso solo tendrá un impacto real si se traduce en más recursos, mayor estabilidad financiera y reglas más claras para repartir el dinero. La discusión no es, por tanto, una simple pugna entre operadores de televisión: es una negociación sobre el modelo económico del FPC. El reclamo de Tulio Gómez no surge de manera aislada. A mediados de 2026, ocho clubes tradicionales del fútbol colombiano —Atlético Nacional, Millonarios, América de Cali, Deportivo Cali, Independiente Santa Fe, Junior, Independiente Medellín y Once Caldas— conformaron el llamado G8 y cuestionaron públicamente la forma actual en que se reparte el dinero de los derechos de televisión entre los 36 equipos profesionales. El grupo sostiene que el sistema vigente no refleja adecuadamente la relevancia deportiva, histórica, comercial y mediática de los clubes más grandes. Su objetivo es conseguir una fórmula que reconozca de manera más directa el aporte de esos equipos a la audiencia, la competencia, la venta de abonos, la asistencia a estadios y el valor de marca del campeonato. En la práctica, esto plantea una tensión evidente: los clubes grandes buscan una mayor participación proporcional, mientras que los equipos de menor peso económico y deportivo defienden un reparto más equilibrado que garantice sostenibilidad para toda la competencia. La discusión interna habría incluido al menos tres fórmulas de distribución. Una de ellas contempla destinar el 90% de los recursos bajo un criterio de base y el 10% restante según la campaña deportiva de cada club; sin embargo, esa alternativa no contaría con el respaldo del G8. La diferencia es importante. Un modelo de “base” tiende a proteger a todos los equipos con un ingreso mínimo, pero puede mantener una brecha reducida entre instituciones con realidades comerciales muy distintas. Una fórmula con mayor peso deportivo o comercial, en cambio, premia a los clubes que más aportan a la taquilla, la audiencia y el interés general por el torneo. El debate, entonces, no es solo sobre cuánto dinero entra, sino sobre qué criterios deben prevalecer: solidaridad entre los 36 clubes, mérito deportivo, tamaño de la hinchada, impacto mediático, historia del club o una combinación de todos esos factores. Los derechos de televisión son una de las fuentes más estables de ingresos para los clubes del fútbol profesional colombiano. En un contexto de costos crecientes, dificultades para captar patrocinios y dependencia de la venta de jugadores, el dinero que llega por transmisiones puede determinar la capacidad de un equipo para competir, pagar nóminas, mantener infraestructura y planificar a mediano plazo. Actualmente, los 36 clubes afiliados a la Dimayor recibirían cerca de 1,2 millones de dólares por temporada bajo el modelo de distribución vigente. La comparación con otros mercados ilustra la dimensión del problema: en Brasil, clubes como Flamengo han llegado a percibir alrededor de 50 millones de dólares anuales por televisión. No se trata de replicar mecánicamente el modelo brasileño, pues las economías, audiencias y estructuras comerciales son diferentes. Pero la brecha explica por qué los dirigentes colombianos ven en el nuevo contrato una oportunidad histórica para aumentar los ingresos del sistema y, al mismo tiempo, discutir una distribución más justa o más competitiva. La defensa de Win Sports no se basa únicamente en su oferta económica. El operador ha estado vinculado a la transmisión del FPC desde 2012 y, durante ese periodo, ha desarrollado una infraestructura de producción, cobertura y comercialización que resulta difícil de reemplazar de inmediato. Para quienes apoyan su continuidad, cambiar de operador podría implicar riesgos operativos: adaptación tecnológica, renegociación de señales, cambios en la producción de partidos y ajustes en la forma en que el público accede a los contenidos. También pesa la experiencia acumulada en la transmisión de un campeonato con múltiples divisiones, sedes y exigencias logísticas. A ello se suma que el nuevo contrato no se limita a la televisión tradicional. Las propuestas contemplan distribución digital, streaming, aplicaciones, contenidos para mercados internacionales y la posibilidad de que terceros sublicencien partidos para ampliar el alcance del campeonato. El fútbol colombiano llega a esta negociación en un momento en que el consumo audiovisual ha cambiado radicalmente. Ya no basta con vender una señal lineal: las audiencias esperan contenidos en múltiples pantallas, resúmenes, programas, archivos, partidos en vivo por internet y productos pensados para redes sociales. Por eso, la próxima licencia tendrá que definir con precisión cómo se comercializarán y distribuirán los partidos. La propuesta externa que recibió la Dimayor contemplaba, además de televisión cerrada, plataformas digitales y streaming, así como la posibilidad de sublicenciar contenidos para ampliar la presencia del torneo dentro y fuera del país. Para los clubes, esto abre una oportunidad: si el FPC logra monetizar mejor sus contenidos digitales, podría aumentar sus ingresos sin depender exclusivamente de la televisión tradicional. Pero también exige garantías sobre producción, derechos, exclusividades, control de datos y reparto de las nuevas fuentes de facturación.

articles.title: CM Punk Shades Seth Rollins in Comment on Charlotte Flair's Photo Ahead of WWE Survivor Series
articles.summary: CM Punk's disdain for Seth Rollins spilled over into his social media activity on Friday.
articles.body:
CM Punk's disdain for Seth Rollins spilled over into his social media activity on Friday.

Commenting on an Instagram post made by Charlotte Flair regarding her WarGames team for Survivor Series, Punk wrote, "This looks cool. I remember when my team had no b---hes on it."

In his comment, Punk was clearly referencing the addition of Seth Rollins to Team USA for the traditional, five-on-five elimination match.

After Cody Rhodes was named the captain for Team USA ahead of its match against Team Mexico at Survivor Series, Punk joined the team and made himself the de facto co-captain.

Rhodes and Punk worked together to bring Je'Von Evans and LA Knight onto the team, but they struggled to find a fifth member, as "Hacksaw" Jim Duggan dropped out and Trick Williams got injured.

Because of that, Punk put his trust in Rhodes to round out the team, and Cody did so this week on Raw by revealing Rollins as the final member.

Punk's facial expression went from joy to dread, and he exited the ring in anger when Rollins arrived.

Since Punk returned to WWE in November 2023, he has been at odds with Rollins, as they have been constant rivals and faced each other in several high-profile matches.

Rollins even cashed in his Money in the Bank contract on Punk at SummerSlam 2025 after Punk had beaten Gunther for the World Heavyweight Championship.

While the team of Charlotte, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Bayley and Stephanie Vaquer appears quite harmonious entering Survivor Series, nothing could be further from the truth for Team USA.

articles.title: Players Championship Finals: Gerwyn Price out in first round as Luke Humphries, Michael van Gerwen progress at Minehead
articles.summary: Report as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman all knocked out in first round at Players Championship Finals; watch the World Darts Championship at London's Alexandra Palace, live on Sky Sports from December 11-January 3
articles.body:
Price was beaten by 6-4 Sebastian Bialecki - the first time the Pole had beaten the Welshman in his career - while Jeffery de Graaf won two legs on the bounce to consign van Veen to defeat by the same scoreline.

Nijman was upset by 20-year-old Henry Coates despite posting an average of 110 - the second-highest average in Players Championship Finals history.

World No 4 Luke Humphries, meanwhile, battled through his recurring back injury to secure a routine 6-3 victory against Darryl Pilgrim, while Michael van Gerwen withstood Connor Scutt to secure safe passage with a 6-3 first-round win of his own.

Beau Greaves also progressed to the second round with a scrappy 6-3 victory against former Lakeside champion Christian Kist despite a mediocre average of 89.64, and will face Rob Owen in the next round.

Van Veen, Nijman and Price joined James Wade, Gary Anderson, and Rob Cross as six of the top 25 players in the world were eliminated at the first opportunity in the last major before the World Darts Championship, which is live on Sky Sports from December 11th.

Wade was beaten 6-4 by Justin Hood and 2014 winner Anderson slipped to a 6-4 loss against Karel Sedlacek, while Cross fell to a thrilling 6-5 loss to Mickey Mansell.

Top players crumble on night of shock Minehead results

Van Veen - who finished runner-up to Price at the Grand Slam - struggled from the outset and throughout his match, managing only one maximum and checking out a lowly 15% of his finishes.

The Dutchman had three darts at double 16 to keep himself in the tournament, but failed to level the scores at 5-5 before de Graaf ruthlessly produced a 112 checkout to produce the first upset of the round.

Price, fresh off his first major win in four years after three successive final defeats, was heavily favoured against 22-year-old Bialecki, and looked to have rediscovered his tournament-winning form at the perfect moment when he produced a stunning 120 checkout to peg the deficit back to 5-4.

But Bialecki kept his cool and threw for the match, claiming his first career win against Price at the seventh attempt. The Pole will face off against de Graaf in round two.

The status quo was somewhat restored when Humphries and van Gerwen produced characteristically routine wins against lower-ranked opponents, with Humphries silencing doubters by averaging 93.32 in a week dominated by coverage of his injury.

But the show was stolen by Coates. The Derby native overcame his opponent's stellar average by notching an incredible 85.71% checkout success rate to claim victory in only his fourth-ever televised game.

Elsewhere, Stephen Bunting edged into the next round after beating German Max Hopp in a last-leg decider, while Kevin Doets averaged 107.34 in his win over Ritchie Edhouse and Chris Dobey came from behind to beat Mike De Decker 6-4.

articles.title: Matvei Michkov Suspension Addressed by Flyers' Rick Tocchet, Status for Islanders Game Revealed
articles.summary: Matvei Michkov will be in the Philadelphia Flyers lineup Saturday against the Islanders after he was held out Friday due to what the Flyers described as an "internal team matter."
articles.body:
Matvei Michkov will be in the Philadelphia Flyers lineup Saturday against the Islanders after he was held out Friday due to what the Flyers described as an "internal team matter."

Head coach Rick Tocchet confirmed Michkov's status after the Flyers' 5-2 Friday evening win over the Vancouver Canucks.

"We have dealt with it and it's over, and that's what it is. And Mich will be in the lineup tomorrow, and that's it," Tocchet said (h/t Sports Radio WIP's Dave Uram). "You deal with it. We've dealt with it. That's it, and you move on. Things happen sometimes."

The Flyers announced about an hour and a half before Friday's 3 p.m. ET puck drop Michkov would not be in the lineup against the Canucks.

The team is set to drop the puck Saturday evening at 7:30 p.m. ET against the visiting Islanders.

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Friday evening Michkov's scratch was due to "a violation of team rules."

"I think some of those things, the organization, you deal with it inside. You don't air it out in the public. That's why," Tocchet said about the lack of detail regarding why Michkov had been scratched. "I think that's the way you approach it."

Tocchet concluded, "It's like any young player. At one point, it happens. You learn from it. We all learn from our mistakes. That's how you deal with things."

When asked if he was concerned there would be any lingering negativity in the locker room, Tocchet said, "No. He was in there high-fiving the guys after the win. No, I don't think so at all."

Flyers forward Sean Couturier, when asked about the team's relationship with Michkov after the game, said: "Listen, we just won a big game, so how about we talk about this big win and how we responded? It's something that I guess is getting resolved internally."

Michkov led the Flyers with both 11 goals and 20 points heading into Friday's game.

The Flyers pivoted to play 11 forwards and seven defensemen due to Michkov's late scratch. Defenseman Owen Tippett was then ruled out with a lower-body injury shortly after taking the ice for warm-ups.

Philadelphia still outshot the visiting Canucks, who are on a three-game losing streak, 29-20 in the win.

"It was business as usual. That's the way we approached it," Tocchet said.

Tocchet also addressed chants, both against him and in support of Michkov, that took place during the Friday home game.

"When you're a head coach this long, you're going to be a target sometimes, and that's the way it is... The chants and stuff, you've got to block it out, right?What are you going to do?" Tocchet said.

Michkov's relationship with Tocchet has already been under scrutiny since the Flyers denied a report from ESPN's Kevin Weekes that Michkov "would likely want a new start elsewhere."

His return to the lineup for the second half of the Flyers' weekend back-to-back could indicate the team is hoping to maintain their relationship with the 21-year-old pending RFA before making a decision on his expiring contract this spring.

articles.body: Alexander Ovechkin's Florida property investment took an unexpected turn after a dispute over water damage reportedly pushed the NHL superstar into a fresh real estate purchase. The Washington Capitals captain had spent years owning a luxury apartment in Florida, but a costly flooding incident and a legal battle with a neighbour added an unusual chapter to his property story. He eventually bought another condo in the same complex for approximately $2.1 million, despite the trouble surrounding his earlier home.Alex Ovechkin's $2.1 million Florida condo purchase followed flooding disputeAlex Ovechkin reportedly purchased the new apartment in the Jade Beach condominium complex in Florida for around $2.1 million in July 2026. The property was located on the 40th floor and offered approximately 2,390 square feet of living space, including four bedrooms.The purchase came after years of trouble involving his original apartment in the same building. Reports said Ovechkin had bought that property in 2016 for approximately $1.9 million. However, a water leak reportedly damaged the luxury residence in 2019 after a plumbing problem involving a neighbouring apartment.The incident led to a dispute over responsibility for the damage. Ovechkin reportedly sought $30,000 in compensation, claiming that the flooding affected his property and caused financial losses. The apartment was also reported to have generated around $10,500 in monthly rental income.Rather than leaving the complex altogether, the hockey star eventually moved forward with another purchase nearby. Reports also noted that the new apartment featured moisture-resistant flooring, a detail that attracted attention given the history of the earlier property.Ovechkin's Florida property dispute ended in settlementThe legal disagreement reportedly continued for several years before both sides reached a settlement in July 2026. The exact terms remained undisclosed, meaning there was no confirmed figure showing how much Ovechkin ultimately received.The dispute highlighted the risks that can come with owning high-value properties, even in luxury residential buildings. Water damage can affect more than interiors and furnishings. It can also disrupt rental arrangements, create repair costs and lead to lengthy disagreements between property owners.For Ovechkin, the reported $2.1 million purchase marked another major Florida real estate move. articles.title: WWE's Bronson Reed Dies at Age 38 'Due to Medical Complications' Following Crown Jewel
articles.summary: WWE announced Friday that veteran wrestler Bronson Reed died at the age of 38.
articles.body:
WWE announced Friday that veteran wrestler Bronson Reed died at the age of 38.

Reed, whose real name was Jermaine Haley, died due to "medical complications," according to WWE's statement on the matter.

Two weeks ago, Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t WrestlePurists ) reported that Reed suffered broken ribs and a lacerated kidney at the Crown Jewel premium live event in Saudi Arabia on Nov. 7.

Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp was the first to report that Reed had suffered an injury at Crown Jewel, which forced him to remain in Saudi Arabia even after other WWE wrestlers and staff flew home to the United States.

Reed was reportedly accompanied by a "top international executive and a member of [WWE's] medical team."

While Reed did not wrestle a match at Crown Jewel, he did interfere during a World Tag Team Championship bout between The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory, and the team of Penta and Je'Von Evans.

Reed brawled with Oba Femi, leading to him getting tossed off the stage and through some tables by Femi.

Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter reported that Reed was injured on that particular spot.

Alvarez (h/t WrestlePurists ) reported last week that Reed had made it back home from Saudi Arabia and was "continuing his recovery from surgery."

Reed is perhaps best known to wrestling fans for his two stints in WWE from 2019 to 2021 and 2022 to 2026.

During his first WWE run, the Aussie was a one-time North American champion in WWE.

Following his release and stops in New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Impact Wrestling, Reed re-signed with WWE in 2022 and did some of the best work of his career in the years that followed.

On the strength of his devastating Tsunami splash finisher, Reed scored victories over several big names, including Roman Reigns and Seth Rollins, and won the 2024 Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal.

Since 2025, Reed had been a member of The Vision, which initially included Breakker, Rollins and Paul Heyman, and later Theory, Logan Paul and Maxxine Dupri.

Reed also wrestled for other promotions in his native Australia and across the world under the names Jonah Rock, Jonah and J-Rock.

He is survived by his daughter and his wife, who is pregnant with the couple's second child.
