articles.title: WWE SmackDown Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights Before Survivor Series WarGames 2026
articles.summary: The go-home SmackDown before Saturday's Survivor Series PLE featured both a title match and Friendsgiving hosted by Danhausen.
articles.body:
The go-home SmackDown before Saturday's Survivor Series PLE featured both a title match and Friendsgiving hosted by Danhausen.

Here is a look at the card from this week's show:

Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley vs. Michin and B-Fab

Sami Zayn and Gunther vs. Kevin Owens and Finn Balor

This week's SmackDown was filmed after Monday's Raw to give the roster and crew time with their families for the holiday, but WWE made sure a handful of big stars were included in the hopes fans would still tune into the pre-taped show.

Let's take a look at what happened on this week's SmackDown.

WWE aired a short tribute before the show to Bronson Reed, whose death was confirmed by WWE earlier today. Rest in peace, Bronson.

CM Punk came to the ring looking much less excited than he has in recent weeks, and it's all due to Seth Rollins joining Team USA. Cody Rhodes soon joined him in the ring to discuss the issues between Punk and Rollins. He said he shouldn't have to apologize for bringing in Rollins because he is going to help them win.

As Punk was ranting, Rollins' music hit, and he came out with the 2x4 that was given to Punk by Jim Duggan last week. He said it was good to be back, and it was good to feel needed by Team USA. The Visionary seemed like he was trying to play nice, but he mentioned AJ Lee and Punk got upset. LA Knight came out to add his thoughts to the mix.

The Megastar tried to rally the troops and told Punk he only has to put up with Seth for one night. Je'Von Evans came out to complete the team. He did a good job giving everyone a pep talk, but it got tense again when Rollins talked a bunch of trash. Punk shook Cody's hand and said he would see him tomorrow.

On any other night, this would have been a pretty decent segment, but it was so hard to get into this just minutes after WWE talked about Reed. It put a damper on everything, which is not the fault of the talent who taped this show on Monday, but it still made it hard to care about the segment.

Punk asking if Rhodes was on crack for thinking Rollins revolutionized the business was kind of funny.

The amount of history between Rhodes, Punk and Rollins made it so easy for them to tell this story.

Evans' was pretty funny in his part of the segment.

The Baddies vs. Bliss and Paxley (Women's Tag Team Championships)

Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley had a chance to regain the tag titles from Michin and B-Fab in the first match on Friday's show. Charlotte Flair and Jade Cargill were at ringside to support their respective allies ahead of tomorrow's WarGames match, which will include five of the six women in and around the ring.

These four women have competed in several tag and six-woman bouts in recent months, so they know each other well and have developed some chemistry as opponents.

Michin and Bliss are both considered veterans at this point in their careers, so when they were in the ring together, things were noticeably smoother than when B-Fab and Paxley were working.

As expected, The Storm and The Queen got into a fight at ringside, but it didn't have a big impact on the outcome. Bliss hit Michin with Sister Abigail to get a relatively clean win and regain the tag titles.

The match had good energy, and a title change is always fun. The post-match attack by Fatal Influence helped push tomorrow's WarGames match, but it cut Bliss and Paxley's celebration short.

Result: Bliss and Paxley defeated Michin and B-Fab

It must take a lot of work and dye to keep B-Fab's hair looking that red.

It's wild that this is the sixth time Bliss has been a tag team champion. Raquel Rodriguez is the only other woman with that many reigns.

B-Fab has been more aggressive recently, which has definitely been helpful for her.

The next match saw Chelsea Green take on a woman who has been a constant thorn in her side recently, Blake Monroe.

As soon as the bell rang, Green ran at Monroe and they started grappling. They rolled out of the ring where Blake threw Chelsea into the announcer's table, but Green returned the favor immediately.

It feels like WWE has put Green through the wringer. She lost her WWE title, her Crown Jewel ring was stolen by the woman who betrayed her and took the title, and she has been repeatedly attacked backstage for no reason.

Tiffany Stratton showed up to pour salt in the wound and taunt Green, but she didn't try to interfere right away. As soon as Green scored the victory, Tiffy and Blake attacked her. Paige ran to the ring to make the save and help Chelsea fend them off.

It felt like the match was just getting interesting when it came to an end. With a little more time, they could have put on a much better show.

We got to see some highlights from Danhausen's Friendsgiving celebration.

Monroe is doing her best to come up with an interesting entrance, but nothing has been as good as what she was doing in NXT yet.

articles.summary: Before Serena and Venus Williams became two of tennis's biggest names, their family home in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, held memories of a very different
articles.body: Before Serena and Venus Williams became two of tennis's biggest names, their family home in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, held memories of a very different life. Nearly three decades after Richard Williams bought the property, the four-bedroom house became the centre of a bitter financial and legal dispute. In April 2024, a judge dismissed another bankruptcy filing by Richard's wife, Lakeisha Williams, leaving the property exposed to foreclosure. The case involved an estimated $600,000 debt, a disputed loan and allegations surrounding the transfer of the family home.Serena Williams' childhood home became the centre of a $600,000 debt disputeRichard Williams reportedly purchased the property in 1995 for approximately $355,000. The house later became closely linked to the early years of Serena and Venus, who trained under their father's guidance before reaching the top of professional tennis.However, the family's history with the property took a difficult turn after Lakeisha faced mounting financial problems. Court proceedings involved allegations that she had forged Richard's signature to transfer the house into her name and secure a loan of approximately $279,000 from lender David Simon.The money was reportedly intended to support a trucking business, which eventually failed. Lakeisha disputed aspects of the allegations and said she had struggled to provide for herself and her son. The debt reportedly grew to around $600,000 after interest and other costs.The property was valued at approximately $1.4 million. Lakeisha had attempted to protect it through bankruptcy proceedings, but the court dismissed her latest Chapter 13 filing in April 2024. She had also struggled to maintain a proposed repayment plan requiring monthly payments of around $10,000.Serena and Venus Williams' family home was eventually soldThe bankruptcy ruling initially raised the prospect that the property would be sold to repay creditors. However, the story took another turn before the planned auction.In August 2024, the house was reportedly sold for approximately $1.2 million to Hardy Firm LLC. Reports said the sale helped settle around $436,000 in outstanding debt, preventing the property from going through the planned foreclosure auction.The identity and connections of the buyer also attracted attention. The Sun reported links between the company and people associated with Lakeisha, although those connections did not establish who ultimately controlled the property.The family dispute also appeared to ease. Later reports said Richard and Lakeisha had reconciled and resumed living together, despite years of legal conflict.For Serena and Venus, the property remained part of the story of their early lives. But the financial battle showed how a home associated with a sporting legacy could become entangled in years of debt, allegations and family disagreements.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: WWE star Bronson Reed, whose real name was Jermaine Haley, has died at 38, leaving behind his wife, Paige, and their young daughter, Deja.
articles.body: WWE star Bronson Reed, whose real name was Jermaine Haley, has died at 38, leaving behind his wife, Paige, and their young daughter, Deja. While wrestling fans remember him for his incredible strength and commanding presence inside the ring, his life outside WWE revolved around the people who stood beside him through years of challenges. From a teenage romance that turned into marriage to an emotional IVF journey and the joy of becoming a father, Reed's family played a major role in his personal and professional journey.Who is Bronson Reed's wife Paige? Their love story began in high schoolPaige Haley was part of Reed's life long before he became a recognised WWE performer. The couple began dating during their high school years and eventually married in May 2021.Their relationship survived the uncertain early years of his wrestling career, including financial difficulties and long periods away from home. Paige also helped him take his first steps towards becoming a professional wrestler.In a 2021 interview with PWInsider, Reed spoke about the support he received from his wife and how she stood by him when his career was still taking shape."She was the one person always stuck by my side and supported me becoming a pro wrestler, being an independent pro wrestler, going to Japan, all the time away to hopefully realize my dream of getting into WWE."The couple also faced personal challenges while trying to start a family. They eventually turned to in vitro fertilisation (IVF), a journey Reed openly discussed with fans in August 2023.When he revealed that the treatment had been successful and they were expecting a daughter, he made sure to recognise Paige's strength throughout the process."Thank you to all of those that reached out when I spoke about the IVF journey my wife and I have been on.Paige has been an absolute rock star through the whole process and is truly my hero.We were successful and are expecting a baby girl! During his 2021 PWInsider interview, he spoke about sharing important career moments with them. articles.summary: Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley struck a major blow ahead of their WarGames match at Survivor Series, beating Michin and B-Fab for the WWE Women's Tag Team Championships on Friday night's episode of SmackDown.
articles.body:
Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley struck a major blow ahead of their WarGames match at Survivor Series, beating Michin and B-Fab for the WWE Women's Tag Team Championships on Friday night's episode of SmackDown.

However, they couldn't enjoy their success for very long as Fatal Influence attacked the celebrating Bliss, Paxley and Charlotte Flair from behind ahead of the Women's WarGames match on Saturday.

Final Picks for WWE Survivor Series WarGames 🔮

Stephanie Vaquer and Bayley ran to the ring in defense of their WarGames teammates, but they were on the wrong end of this battle as Michin, B-Fab and Jade Cargill also got involved and ultimately stood victorious in the ring with Fatal Influence, setting up a tense Saturday showdown.

Michin and B-Fab had beaten Bliss and Paxley for the women's tag team titles on the Oct. 23 edition of SmackDown, but Alexa and Tatum got the belts back by winning their rematch on Friday.

The victory gave Bliss and Paxley some significant momentum prior to the five-on-five WarGames match they are scheduled to partake in on Saturday.

Bliss and Paxley are set to team with Charlotte Flair, Bayley and Stephanie Vaquer against Jade Cargill, Michin and Fatal Influence's Jacy Jayne, Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid at Survivor Series.

In August, Paxley made her WWE main roster debut and joined forces with Bliss and Flair in their rivalry with Cargill, Michin and B-Fab.

Two months later, Bliss and Paxley became women's tag team champions together for the first time when they beat Henley and Reid.

Their reign lasted only about two weeks before dropping the titles to Michin and B-Fab, but Alexa and Tatum are now back atop the women's tag team division.

Additionally, Bliss made history with the win on Friday, as she tied Raquel Rodriguez for the most all-time WWE Women's Tag Team Championship reigns with six.

Should Bliss and Paxley come out on top in WarGames at Survivor Series as well, it will complete a perfect Thanksgiving weekend for the new champs.

articles.title: Ducks lose momentum of early Solberg strikes, can't find push against Kings
articles.summary: Anaheim led the league in comeback wins last season, but are 3-3-0 when tied after two and 1-10-0. Solberg scored first two NHL goals in Norwegian showcase.
articles.body:
ANAHEIM, Calif. – In a game that turned all hockey-watching eyes of Norway toward Honda Center, the Anaheim Ducks squandered a strong start against their rivals and could not make a late push.

Stian Solberg scored his first two NHL goals in the first period, but countryman Mats Zuccarello matched with two sharp-angle goals in the second period. The Los Angeles Kings grabbed the lead on an early third-period deflection and held off the Ducks, 5-3, on Friday at Honda Center.

Anaheim (12-13-1, 25 points) has lost seven of its last nine following a five-game winning streak. This was just the Ducks' fourth total loss when scoring three or more goals (12-3-1), and they are winless when scoring two or fewer (0-11-0).

"We got ourselves on our heels there early in the second," Joel Quenneville said. "They scored two goals, funny goals, and they slowed down the pace. We were skating well in the first period, and I think we got standing around there a bit."

Anaheim, kings of the late-game comeback last season, are just 3-3-0 when tied after two periods and 1-10-0 when trailing after 40 minutes. The Ducks–who thought they had scored with the goalie pulled, but the referees blew the play dead and upheld that call on review–are second in the NHL in extra-attacker goals with five, but each has come in a regulation loss.

"We haven't been able to do that lately," Mikael Granlund said. "We've got to find another gear when it comes time. Something we gotta do better."

"I don't think that's the recipe for being successful," Quenneville said, "coming back late in games thinking that's going to work. Eventually it can catch up to you. Certainly, we were charmed in some of those games last year."

After a traditionally sleepy start to this traditional Black Friday matinee, Stian Solberg woke up Honda Center with his first two deposits on his NHL ledger.

Mikael Granlund sliced the defensive zone with a diagonal pass to Solberg at the right point, where the Norwegian faked out countryman Mats Zuccarello and ripped a shot far side around the kneeling King for the lead, 1-0.

"That was a special moment for me," Solberg said, "and a lot of fun to put that in the back of the net. That's probably something I'm going to remember for a long time… It was kind of funny it was him. I'm probably going to shoot (Zuccarello) a text."

Solberg's first career NHL goal put him as the third Norwegian defenseman to score an NHL goal, joining Emil Lilleberg and Ole-Kristian Tollefsen. Lilleberg, currently on the Tampa Bay blue line, has scored five in his NHL career, and Tollefsen netted four for the Columbus Blue Jackets.

Solberg, just the 11th Norwegian in NHL history, was clearly feeling it, as he notched another just 76 second later. The 20-year-old wound up for a blast from the left point, hesitated and fired through traffic for his second career NHL strike, 2-0.

Those are the fastest two goals scored by a Ducks defenseman in franchise history and the seventh-fastest two goals by a rookie defenseman in the NHL since 1944.

Beckett Sennecke in his return from a week's stint on injured reserve tied up the game with a five-on-three one-timer fed by Granlund in the second period, 3-3.

Not to be outdone by his young countryman, veteran Norwegian Mats Zuccarello evened things up for Los Angeles early in the second period, and both from near impossible angles.

Just over a minute in from below the goal line in the left corner, Zuccarello shot off Laurent Brossoit's skates and in, 2-1. Four minutes later from the goal line in the right corner, Zuccarello buzzed the tower and ripped one by Brossoit's ear to tie the game, 2-2.

This was the first time in NHL history that two Norwegians scored in the same game and passed up hat tricks from Zuccarello and former Mighty Duck Espen Knutsen as the most goals by Norwegians in one NHL game.

The Kings pushed for the go-ahead goal twice.

Three minutes after Zuccarello's second goal, Adrian Kempe popped in a rebound, 3-2, as Solberg blocked a point shot but screened Brossoit.

Two minutes into the third period, Anders Lee deflected a Brian Dumoulin point shot around a metric ton of traffic in front of the Ducks net to regain the lead, 4-3.

Laurent Brossoit stopped 17 of 21 shots in his seventh start of the season.

"We didn't give up much," Quenneville said. "That still has to be the recipe… I didn't mind how we played."

Quenneville confirmed postgame that Lukáš Dostál would start the second half of the back-to-back in Los Angeles tomorrow.

Darcy Kuemper made 25 saves for the Kings.

The Ducks (25 points) were jumped for the third and final spot in the Pacific Division, as the San Jose Sharks (12-14-2, 26 points) beat the Vegas Golden Knights, after losing 7-0 in Anaheim on Wednesday. Calgary Flames (11-14-2, 24 points) lost in New Jersey, and Seattle Kraken (11-11-1, 23 points) play in Edmonton tonight.

After tonight, Seattle still played four fewer games than Anaheim and Calgary and five fewer than San Jose.

Los Angeles (9-12-2, 20 points) is lurking with the same amount of games played as Seattle.

Anaheim finishes off the second half of a Thanksgiving weekend home-and-home with the Los Angeles Kings up at Crypto.com Arena on Saturday. The Ducks host the league-leading Minnesota Wild on Tuesday.

Solberg became the third Norwegian to ever record a multi-goal game in the NHL. The first was done by former Mighty Duck Espen Knutsen with the Columbus Blue Jackets in Anaheim on Feb. 25, 2001. Zuccarello netted his 25th career multi-goal game on Friday in Anaheim.

Cutter Gauthier remains one goal behind the NHL record for goals in a month with one game to play in November on Saturday in Los Angeles. Gauthier has 19 goals this month, and Teemu Selanne (1992) and Joe Malone (1921) hold the record with 20.

Leo Carlsson and Beckett Sennecke swapped spots on and off of injured reserve on Friday morning. Carlsson (day-to-day, upper-body) went on IR retroactive to his injury on Nov. 21 to open a roster spot, and Sennecke came off IR to play against Los Angeles. Sennecke missed three games with an upper-body injury.

Ryan Poehling (long-term injured reserve, MCL sprain) was a full participant in practice on Thursday. He has been skating with the team for a week, his seventh week of a 6-8 week recovery timeline. Quenneville said postgame that Poehling was a "maybe" for tomorrow in Los Angeles.

Sam Colangelo, Tyson Hinds and Ville Husso were tonight's healthy scratches.

articles.title: Important warning emerges for all teams pursuing Simon Edvinsson
articles.summary: A new concern could complicate Detroit's efforts to move him before the deadline.
articles.body:
The trade speculation surrounding Simon Edvinsson continues to heat up, but a new report suggests that landing the Detroit Red Wings defenseman may be considerably more complicated than interested teams initially anticipated.

With the Dec. 1 deadline approaching, several NHL clubs have reportedly been monitoring Edvinsson's situation. The Edmonton Oilers have emerged as a particularly intriguing potential destination, while the Boston Bruins have also been mentioned as a team to watch.

However, according to a recent report, there is one major obstacle standing in the way of a potential blockbuster deal: Edvinsson's next contract.

Speaking about the situation, Elliotte Friedman explained that he isn't convinced the defenseman would necessarily agree to sign with every team that has been connected to him. More importantly, several interested clubs reportedly want assurances that they can secure Edvinsson on a long-term contract before giving up significant assets to acquire him.

"There are a couple of places they've talked more about a bridge than a long-term deal," the insider explained, adding that teams aren't willing to surrender valuable players without a longer commitment from the Swedish defenseman.

That creates a difficult situation for Detroit. The Red Wings may be able to find interested trade partners, but those clubs could be reluctant to meet the asking price without knowing exactly what they're getting in return.

Edvinsson has established himself as an important part of Detroit's blue line, making him a valuable trade target. However, his contract situation makes any potential deal considerably riskier.

For Edmonton and the other teams reportedly keeping tabs on the situation, the question is no longer simply whether they can acquire Edvinsson. It's whether they can convince him to stay for the long haul.

With the deadline approaching, that uncertainty could become the biggest obstacle in what has quickly turned into one of the NHL's most intriguing trade stories.

His combination of size, toughness and willingness to play a physical game gives New York an added element that opponents have to account for every night.

articles.title: Blue Jackets shut out by Red Wings, booed: 'You've got to push back'
articles.summary: The Columbus Blue Jackets continue to flounder offensively, drawing boos at Nationwide Arena after shutout loss to Detroit Red Wings.
articles.body:
The booing began with just under three minutes left Nov. 27 at Nationwide Arena. It emanated from the upper reaches of the building and cascaded to the ice during the Blue Jackets' 2-0 loss to the Detroit Red Wings .

Down two goals, the Blue Jackets had just sent goalie Jet Greaves to the bench for a last gasp 6-on-5 advantage that fans quickly realized was an exercise in futility, much like the home team's play throughout its Black Friday matinee.

See highlights from Blue Jackets vs. Red Wings NHL hockey

Things went as expected from there, ending with the Red Wings finally putting an end to a torturous afternoon. Neither team was good, but the Blue Jackets (9-14-1) were, by far, worse.

It was their third straight loss, fifth straight loss at home and they're 10 points out of a playoff spot on Thanksgiving weekend, which has become a benchmark for most the NHL's eventual playoff field. Saying the collective mood of the Blue Jackets right now is grim is putting it kindly.

There are 60 games remaining and Columbus is lacking two things that typically go arm-in-arm: a pulse and goals. Remarkably, this was the first time they Jackets have been shut out this season despite ranking last in the NHL while scoring 2.33 goals per game.

"It's impossible not to think about it," center Adam Fantilli said. "Like, we can hear our fans booing. It's not like we're deaf. Like, we understand the situation. We understand how frustrating it is for them. We're just as frustrated. We're trying to figure it out. We're trying to do everything we can, and it's not going for us."

The problem, as seen from the seats, press box and television broadcast, is that it often doesn't look like the Blue Jackets are doing everything they can. Too many times, they look like a team playing out the string, and their level of pushback looks empty.

An opposing player lights up a teammate with a cheap shot and the ice doesn't become a yard sale of discarded gloves and sticks. An opposing team sets out to keep the Blue Jackets out of the most dangerous scoring areas and finds it all too easy to accomplish.

That's without mentioning the litany of fumbled passes, pucks hopping over sticks, passes sent into a teammate's skates, passes sent to nobody in particular and shots that accomplish nothing but dusting snow off the puck.

All of these afflictions were on full display against the Red Wings, who used their impressive size on the back end to clog up the middle of their defensive zone and push the Blue Jackets to the perimeter most of the game. The result was a glaring statistical anomaly on the scoresheet, which showed the Red Wings with a 21-18 edge in shots and the Jackets with a 62-42 edge in attempts.

"I think part of it's a credit to them," Blue Jackets defenseman Zach Werenski said. "They did a good job of standing in our [shooting] lanes, but we've got to find a way to get pucks to the net, get second and third chances, and find a way to score. We had possession, we had some looks, but I feel like when a team like that's fronting [the net] like they are, we've got to get pucks near the blue [paint] and try to find goals that way."

If that sounds familiar, there's a good reason. The Blue Jackets have said either that exact same thing or something similar to it all season long. They keep saying it, as a team that president/general manager Don Waddell, intentionally packed with bigger bodies, and it's still not happening.

Either the Blue Jackets don't get anywhere near the opposing net to scrap for rebounds or they get there without any shots getting through. It's a conundrum they haven't come close to solving, which has cast a feeling of hopelessness around this season.

There's 60 mores games left. Are most going to go like this?

How many times are the Blue Jackets going to let down a building full of their fans with lackluster performances, continually testing the limits of supporters who've are among the most patient and loyal groups in North American professional sports?

Sitting among Blue Jackets fans this time were their dads, including Johnny Gaudreau's dad, Guy. It was the start of the Blue Jackets' fathers weekend, which will include a trip to Pittsburgh on Nov. 30 to open a four-game trip that follows with games against the Carolina Hurricanes, Nashville Predators and Tampa Bay Lightning.

If there's any hope of salvaging this season left, it must start in Pittsburgh.

"You've got to push back, you've got to fight back," coach Rick Bowness said. "We're going to find out Monday. The only thing that matters is getting ready for Monday."

articles.title: Mangiapane Scores Twice, Blackhawks Beat Rangers For Fourth Straight Win
articles.summary: The Chicago Blackhawks (10-14-2) tied a franchise record for the fewest shots recorded in a regular-season game with 10, but […]
articles.body:
The Chicago Blackhawks (10-14-2) tied a franchise record for the fewest shots recorded in a regular-season game with 10, but it was enough to defeat the New York Rangers (13-11-1) 2-1 at the United Center on Friday.

Andrew Mangiapane scored both of Chicago's goals, his first two tallies of the season, Oliver Moore had two assists, and Spencer Knight stopped 30 of 31 shots as the Blackhawks extended their winning streak to four games. The Blackhawks are now 6-1-1 in eight games since an abysmal 0-3 Southeastern road trip earlier this month.

Mika Zibanejad scored for the Rangers, while Dylan Garand started in net and allowed two goals on 10 shots faced. Adam Fox extended his point streak to five games with an assist on Zibanejad's power-play goal.

All three goals in Friday's game were power-play tallies, with the Blackhawks converting on both opportunities and extending their goal streak to eight games. Since opening the season with a 5-for-51 stretch, the power play has now scored on 13 of its last 22 opportunities.

Even without Patrick Kane and Tyler Bertuzzi , the man advantage continued its red-hot stretch, and it was the second unit stepping up to score both goals against the Rangers. Entering Friday, New York had the NHL's top-ranked penalty kill and had allowed a league-low three power-play goals in their first 12 road games.

But even without their best offensive players, including captain Connor Bedard and Bowen Byram , the power play impressively still found a way to generate all the offense needed against a stout Rangers' PK for a fourth straight win.

Defensively, Knight was outstanding for the second straight game, as the 25-year-old was credited with 2.03 goals saved above expected against the Rangers. Over his last three outings — all wins — Knight has stopped 92 of 97 shots for a .948 save percentage.

While the Rangers outshot and outchanced the Blackhawks by a wide margin, they were credited with only 10 high-danger scoring chances at even strength. Much like Wednesday's win in Seattle, the Hawks' defense didn't allow many threatening looks. The defensemen and forwards also selflessly stepped in the shooting lane, recording 22 blocked shots in Friday's win.

Here are highlights from the Blackhawks 2-1 win over the Rangers, moving their 2026-27 regular-season record to 10-14-2 in 26 games.

With Matt Rempe in the penalty box for boarding Kevin Korchinski , the scorching-hot Blackhawks power play hit the ice for the first time and converted. Moore poked a loose puck over to Mangiapane at the right circle, and he fired a one-timer past Garand for his first goal of the season at 4:23. 1-0, Chicago.

Oliver Moore➡️Andrew Mangiapane🚨 #Blackhawks extend their power-play streak to 8 games, as Moore gets the puck over to Mangiapane for his 1st goal of the season! 1-0. pic.twitter.com/DhTBlwMrNL — Talkin' Hawkey (@TalkinHawkey) November 27, 2026

Oliver Moore➡️Andrew Mangiapane🚨 #Blackhawks extend their power-play streak to 8 games, as Moore gets the puck over to Mangiapane for his 1st goal of the season! 1-0. pic.twitter.com/DhTBlwMrNL

Talkin' Hawkey (@TalkinHawkey) November 27, 2026

Roughly five minutes later, Dillon Boucher made Rempe answer for his hit on Korchinski. The two enforcers dropped the gloves at center ice, with Rempe eventually getting the takedown. They exchanged a few good shots in the quick scrap.

Boucher vs Rempe 🥊 pic.twitter.com/yBxgWQUcgy — BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) November 27, 2026

Boucher vs Rempe 🥊 pic.twitter.com/yBxgWQUcgy

BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) November 27, 2026

Boucher was called for another penalty shortly after leaving the penalty box, sending the Rangers to their second power play of the period. Zibanejad converted to tie the game 1-1 at 17:41, with a one-timer from the slot beating Knight between his legs. Rangers captain JT Miller recorded his 500th career assist with the primary helper.

J.T. with the set up and Mika buries it for the PPG 🤝 pic.twitter.com/2V3maex7Fx — New York Rangers (@NYRangers) November 27, 2026

J.T. with the set up and Mika buries it for the PPG 🤝 pic.twitter.com/2V3maex7Fx

New York Rangers (@NYRangers) November 27, 2026

Just 27 seconds after Zibanejad's goal, Jaroslav Chmelar was called for slashing, sending the Blackhawks power play back on the ice. For the second time in as many attempts, the man advantage converted, with Mangiapane scoring his second goal of the period at 19:07. Moore recorded his second assist. 2-1.

Oliver Moore➡️Ryan Donato➡️Andrew Mangiapane🚨 Donato sets up Mangiapane for his 2nd goal of the period & season! Moore with his 2nd assist of the period. #Blackhawks power play stays red hot! 2-1. pic.twitter.com/HlQGs2rHpu — Talkin' Hawkey (@TalkinHawkey) November 27, 2026

Oliver Moore➡️Ryan Donato➡️Andrew Mangiapane🚨 Donato sets up Mangiapane for his 2nd goal of the period & season! Moore with his 2nd assist of the period. #Blackhawks power play stays red hot! 2-1. pic.twitter.com/HlQGs2rHpu

The Blackhawks took a 2-1 lead into the intermission, converting on two of their three shots. New York led 10-3 in shots on goal and 7-5 in scoring chances in a low-event period. All three goals were scored on the power play.

Neither team found much offensive success in the second period, with the score remaining 2-1 after 40 minutes.

Perhaps the most notable moment of the period was Kantserov blocking a shot in the defensive zone and immediately heading to the dressing room. Vladislav Gavrikov's point shot appeared to hit Kantserov in the left hand. Fortunately, Kantserov returned for the start of the third period.

Roman Kantserov down the tunnel after blocking this shot: pic.twitter.com/YJDRbiTN8c — BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) November 28, 2026

Roman Kantserov down the tunnel after blocking this shot: pic.twitter.com/YJDRbiTN8c

BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) November 28, 2026

The Blackhawks remained ahead 2-1 into the second intermission, but the Rangers led 18-9 in shots on goal and 20-13 in scoring chances.

New York outshot the Blackhawks 13-1 and led 15-1 in scoring chances in the third period, but Knight stood tall and secured the one-goal lead. Mangiapane and Ryan Donato recorded pivotal shot blocks late in the period.

HAWKS WIN! 2-1 FINAL Sure wasn't pretty, but the #Blackhawks extend their winning streak to 4 games. Mangiapane with both goals. Moore with two assists. Knight stops 30 of 31. Now 6-1-1 in the last 8 games! Hawks move to 10-14-2 & are back in action Sunday vs. Minnesota. pic.twitter.com/Nj1lj9Y1wj — Jack Bushman (@JackBushman2) November 28, 2026

HAWKS WIN! 2-1 FINAL Sure wasn't pretty, but the #Blackhawks extend their winning streak to 4 games. Mangiapane with both goals. Moore with two assists. Knight stops 30 of 31. Now 6-1-1 in the last 8 games! Hawks move to 10-14-2 & are back in action Sunday vs. Minnesota. pic.twitter.com/Nj1lj9Y1wj

Jack Bushman (@JackBushman2) November 28, 2026

The final horn sounded at the United Center, signaling the Blackhawks' fourth straight win. The fans in attendance didn't witness the most eventful game, but they at least saw a win! The Hawks return to action next on Sunday against the Minnesota Wild.

articles.title: Central Bucks West shuts out Spring-Ford, wins district championship
articles.summary: CB West shut out Spring-Ford in the PIAA District One Class 6A football championship game. The Bucks advanced to the PIAA state semifinals with the win.
articles.body:
DOYLESTOWN — Central Bucks West played for its sixth PIAA District One football championship on Friday night.

The Bucks won District One onfield titles under Mike Pettine in 1993 and 1997-99, as well as Mike Carey in 2000.

Spring-Ford, like CB West, went into the game at War Memorial Field with identical 12-1 records.

The Bucks finished the job, downing the Rams 34-0 behind a dominant rushing attack and suffocating defense. Senior Lou Cipollo ran for a pair of touchdowns while seniors Nick Miletto and Braylen Cope both scored a rushing touchdown.

CB West will face the St. Joseph Prep/Nazareth winner in next weekend's Class 6A semifinals. Prep led Nazareth 49-20 at the start of the fourth quarter.

West had reached the district title game in 2022, when it lost at Garnet Valley, while Spring-Ford fell to Coatesville for the 2012 district championship. This is the Bucks' first district title in 26 seasons.

Rob Rowan's CB West squad defeated Perkiomen Valley 56-42, Central Bucks East 44-21 and Council Rock South 30-13 to reach the final, while Spring-Ford topped Quakertown 42-28, Plymouth Whitemarsh 28-21 and top-seeded Downingtown East 17-14 at districts.

*Check back later tonight for much more on the game.

What's next for Central Bucks West Football?

The Bucks will face St. Joseph Prep or Nazareth in the state semifinals next weekend.

articles.title: Men’s hockey: Gophers blank Mavericks
articles.summary: Luca Di Pasquo stopped all 28 shots he to backstop the Minnesota men’s hockey team to a 3-0 victory over Minnesota State in a nonconference game Friday night...
articles.body:
Luca Di Pasquo stopped all 28 shots he to backstop the Minnesota men's hockey team to a 3-0 victory over Minnesota State in a nonconference game Friday night at 3M Arena at Mariucci.

Brodie Ziemer scored to give the Gophers (6-4-3 overall, 1-1-2 Big Ten) a 1-0 lead in the first period, and Axel Begley and Wyatt Cullen added insurance goals in the first game of a home-and-home series against the Mavericks (4-8-3 overall, 2-3-3 CCHA).

"I thought we did a really good job of managing our emotions and playing the right way throughout," Gophers coach Brett Larson said. "You've got to earn everything against (Minnesota State), and I thought our guys didn't get frustrated by that. I thought they just kept sticking to it and playing the right way. And we were finally rewarded for it."

It was the third-straight victory in the series for Minnesota, which has just one loss in its last 10 appearances.

Di Pasquo earned his second shutout with Minnesota and the fourth of his NCAA career. The senior is 3-0-3 with a 1.60 goals-against average and .944 save percentage in his past six starts.

"I thought (Luca) changed the game at the moment we needed him to keep us in the game, and that was huge," Larson said.

The Gophers play their first road game in more than a month when they travel to the Mayo Clinic Health System Event Center in Mankato to close out the series with the Mavericks. Puck drop is set for 6 p.m.

articles.title: Multiple Florida State captains refuse handshakes with Florida at coin toss, raising sportsmanship questions
articles.summary: Florida State Seminoles captains refused handshakes at the coin toss vs the Florida Gators, drawing fan backlash, with only Duce Robinson offering a hand.
articles.body: The day after Thanksgiving kicks off the main slate of rivalry week in college football. Thanksgiving ushered in several days of rivalry matchups, with teams across the country facing their top foes, often in-state rivals. Before Florida and Florida State kicked off in the state's capital city, the rivalry’s intensity was on display in the lead-up to the pregame coin toss. FSU's team captains appeared to decline the customary handshake. Multiple players were seen with their hands behind their backs or at their sides. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Duce Robinson, a Florida State wide receiver who was on crutches, appeared to be the only one of the four Seminoles captains to reach out for handshake at midfield. The exchange sparked fan reactions on social media. "Duce is only class act there. The rest have to go, especially the twins," an FSU fan replied to a video showing the interaction on X. "We aren’t in a position to be acting hard and refusing to dap people up. Bad look," another Noles fan wrote on X. IT TURNS OUT FLORIDA GATORS COACH JON SUMRALL IS JUST AS SUPERSTITIOUS AS HIS FANBASE Once the game kicked off, Florida running back Jadan Baugh's 3-yard touchdown helped lift the No. 20 Gators to a 26-10 win over FSU. Baugh became the first player in program history to record consecutive 1,000-yard rushing seasons. Baugh finished the day with 77 yards for Florida, who have won six of eight games against FSU. Gators quarterback Aaron Philo threw for 127 yards for Florida before leaving because of an injury. Backup Trammel Jones Jr. had a 1-yard touchdown run but also had a fourth-quarter interception. The Seminoles, down to their fifth running back due to injury, managed just 98 total rushing yards. Florida is bowl eligible but will not know its postseason destination until Dec. 6. Florida State’s season is over, and the program will await the arrival of its next head coach, Glenn Schumann, who is not expected to take over full-time in Tallahassee until after No. 1 Georgia’s likely College Football Playoff run ends. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Schumann is Georgia’s defensive coordinator. Georgia will face in-state rival Georgia Tech on Saturday. The Bulldogs have already clinched a spot in what is expected to be the final SEC Championship game. Alabama, Texas and Tennessee are all vying for the second spot in the conference championship game in Atlanta. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: 'Gonna miss our seniors': Lake Travis' emotional season ends with 3rd round playoff loss
articles.summary: One week after rallying for an OT win, Lake Travis fell in a heartbreaker to San Antonio Brennan on Friday in the Class 6A Division I regional semifinals.
articles.body:
SAN MARCOS - Lake Travis was unable to find the score it needed in the final minute of Friday's 24-17 playoff loss to San Antonio Brennan at UFCU Stadium. Brennan (12-1) advances to next week's Region IV-6A Division I final against either Round Rock or San Antonio Harlan.

The Cavaliers (7-4-1), trailing by a touchdown, took over for their final drive at their own 12-yard line with 4 minutes, 56 seconds left in the game. Lake Travis marched methodically down the field to Brennan's 31, but Cavs quarterback Jason Carter , moments after shrugging off a Brennan pass rusher, was strip-sacked by Bears defensive back Josiah Tolefree with less than 30 seconds remaining.

The loss came one week after Lake Travis had rallied to beat Cibolo Steele in overtime.

"I thought we did some things down the stretch that gave us a chance to win the ball game," Cavs head coach Hank Carter said. "We had a guy come free, and I thought Jason shook off the first one, but the second one got us, and then we couldn't hang onto the ball."

Friday's loss concluded a roller coaster season that showcased the resilience of the Lake Travis program. The Cavaliers were met with tragedy before the season opened when senior offensive lineman Odin Hensley died in August. The Cavaliers cancelled their season opener against Dripping Springs as they grieved.

Banners honoring Hensley have been in the stands at every Lake Travis game. Stickers dedicated to him are on the team's helmets. And every game this season was a 48-minute tribute to the offensive lineman.

For the team, Hensley's death brought them closer together and even galvanized them.

"It helped us take every moment in with each other," senior receiver and defensive back Luca Antoun said. "You never know when something's going to happen to your friend or your teammate, so we just appreciate each other more and never took anything for granted."

The Cavaliers dealt with bumps throughout the season. They tied Cibolo Steele in a Sept. 11 regular-season matchup that was called in the third quarter due to weather. Lake Travis stumbled against San Antonio Cornerstone Christian the following week and again against Cedar Ridge on Oct. 9 on the debut of its newly renovated stadium. Lake Travis also lost by 21 points to archrival Westlake in October, putting their record at 3-3-1.

"We lost several games this year, but we play good people. That can happen," Hank Carter said.

That's when Lake Travis started looking more like the program it's been over the last two decades. The Cavs beat a Round Rock team that also made the third round of the playoffs by 17 points seven days after losing to Westlake, and they concluded the regular season with a 58-0 thumping of Westwood.

The Cavaliers carried that form into the playoffs, taking down Johnson 45-14 in their playoff opener before notching a 39-38 overtime win against Steele in the area round. Jason Carter, who completed 22 of 37 passes for 219 yards and an interception against Brennan, connected with Westin Smith on the game-winning 2-point conversion in that game.

Lake Travis had a chance to follow its win against Steele with another memorable postseason victory Friday. The score was tied 10-10 at the half as the Cavaliers missed a 34-yard field goal in the final minute of the second quarter. Brennan's four-star running back Jayshawn Mitchell gave the Bears a lead with a 60-yard touchdown less than two minutes into the third quarter, his second score of the day. Mitchell finished with 175 yards on 22 carries.

The Cavaliers knotted the score with 3:36 left in the third on Henry Hopping's 1-yard run. It was Lake Travis' second 1-yard touchdown of the day as Teddy Lofgren also found the end zone from the same distance in the second quarter.

The score remained tied until the fourth quarter, when Brennan quarterback Jeremiah Conwell, who only threw 10 passes in the game, found Jaylin Kelly for a 28-yard touchdown on fourth-and-6 with 6:24 left.

"They made a great play," Hank Carter said. "They've got a really good team, so we have to be ready for anything. They executed well in that moment."

Lake Travis had two more possessions after Kelly's touchdown, but were unable to find the score they needed.

Hank Carter believed this was a game the Cavaliers could win. The fact that a group he's fond of doesn't have another game to prepare for is something he hates for his players.

"I'm very proud of our guys," he said. "I'm gonna miss our seniors, and was hoping we could keep it going for a few more weeks."
